subject: Activate Ruff ANN rule for annotations
message:
Activate Ruff ANN rule for annotations

This is fairly similar to what mypy does. The main difference is that
ruff can find some of the issues faster. Aside from the speed when
developing the main benefit is that it can be easier to fix a sub
section of code and resolve some of the issues at a time. The violations
are ignored per section and can be fixed or split apart further as parts
of the code gets changed so that it's in compliance with the typing.

subject: Create permissions and menu items if none previously existed
message:
Create permissions and menu items if none previously existed

The `infrahub db update-core-schema` command will now also create menu
items and permission objects assuming that no previous menu item exists
for the new menu, and the same for permissions if one permission has
been defined this step will be ignored otherwise full permissions will
be assigned to the existing users and the Infrahub Users group will be
created.

This is a bit of a poor mans migration as these type of objects don't
fit into the typical current workflow.

```bash
infrahub db migrate
infrahub db update-core-schema
```

subject: IFC-1050 Add permission manager (#5362)
message:
IFC-1050 Add permission manager (#5362)

This PR introduces the permission manager.

This object is build per user session / per request and is carried over
in the GraphQL context. This allows to fetch permissions only once and
to perform lookups in memory. It is also implemented as a FastAPI dependency
to check for permissions for REST API endpoints.

The permission manager is in charge of loading permissions from the
configured backends. Therefore these backends are now simple constructs
that load permissions from a store before handing them over to the
manager.

The permission manager also takes care of deciding when to grant or
revoke a permission for a user. It also reports permissions for a user
when requested.

Working with the permission framework, from a codebase perspective, should
be greatly improved. Everything (almost) must go through the manager which
exposes utility method for single line (until the code formatter runs) calls.

Fixes #5350

subject: IFC-592 Merge schemas when loading them from files (#5482)
message:
IFC-592 Merge schemas when loading them from files (#5482)

When loading multiple schemas files, they used to be imported one by
one. With this change, the files are now parsed as schemas and then
merged together in order to produce a single schema to load. The merge
is performed one by one in the order of the files. This means that the
schema coming last will overwrite the previous one if they refer to the
same nodes.

subject: IFC-15 Support for mandatory/optional parent relationship (#5561)
message:
IFC-15 Support for mandatory/optional parent relationship (#5561)

Fixes #3682

Makes parent relationship mandatory in some cases.

The parent relationship becomes mandatory if the node depends on another one which is not itself or a generic of itself.

This allows, for instance, to not require a continent to have a parent while enforcing a
country to have a parent continent.

The parent won't be required if a node can depends on one of its own. For instance, an IP prefix can have a parent prefix, which is still optional as an prefix can live on its own.

subject: fix(backend): node_create_all duplicate AttributeValue rels
message:
fix(backend): node_create_all duplicate AttributeValue rels

If there are duplicate AttributeValue nodes present (due to concurrent
node creation for example), the MERGE statement would return more than
one node. Thus the HAS_VALUE relationship would be created for all the
nodes that have been returned.
Due to that behavior, attribute retrieval is slower because more
(duplicate) rows are returned in node_list_get_attribute.

Fix this by using a LIMIT 1 statement right after MERGE.

Using LIMIT 1 implies removing FOREACH statements which are not
compatible with LIMIT (that implies WITH). Move to CALL subqueries
instead to work that around.

CALL subqueries do not work very well with UNWIND when the list is
empty, make the whole query dynamic and remove parts when lists are
empty to work that around.

feat(backend): add database connection throttling

Also add metrics related to in use connection.
First attempt was to use metric callback so that we grab the actual
usage but was hard since we require access to the request context that has the
DB driver object referenced.
A simpler version is to keep track of the last usage value seen and
update the metric accordingly.

Note that the max_concurrent_queries setting should match the query
thread pool on the server side (defaults to 400) and be distributed
among server workers.

message:
IFC-1409 Fix HFID duplicates for component templates (#6218)

When loading several schemas without a restart the logic was adding the
same HFID and uniqueness constraint element more than once for component
templates. This lead to a final schema with unpractical HFID and
uniqueness constraints (mostly from a user perspective). While a restart
would fix the issue, this change makes sure it does not happen between
restarts.

An integration test has also been added to highlight the issue in case
of a regression.

subject: fix(backend): make sure filter subqueries start from the node
message:
fix(backend): make sure filter subqueries start from the node

Without this change, the planner will use the peer node index (either
node uuid or attribute value index) as the starting point of the query.
Thus in the case of IPAM, when we have a single namespace with thousands
of addresses/prefixes, it will start the query from the namespace and
traverse all the addresses/prefixes inside that same namespace (thus
retraversing all addresses for each address...).

Unfortunately, it looks like there's no support to "ignore" an index, so
a little trick here is to filter the actual starting node using its own
uuid to force the planner to use that node as the starting point.

Signed-off-by: ub6b8c92a6359829a <ub6b8c92a6359829a@users.invalid>

template names while in fact, their uniqueness is based on a name and a
parent template.

message:
IFC-1690 Fix available prefixes when parent prefix is empty (#6874)

This change makes sure that we return subnets of the container prefix
for which we asked the available space. When a container prefix has no
space reserved, the next 2 smaller subnets that fit inside the container
must be returned. For instance, if 192.0.2.0/24 has no subnets, the
available space query must report 192.0.2.0/25 and 192.0.2.128/25.

message:
improve profiles docs (#6955)

* improve profiles docs

* update code

* fix: add missing newline at end of profiles topic documentation

* remove comments and toml from docs generation

* add back toml

* fix: import Self from typing_extensions for Python 3.10 compatibility

The GitHub Actions CI pipeline was failing because  was being imported
from  instead of .  was only
introduced in Python 3.11, but the CI uses Python 3.10.

This aligns with the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase where
is imported from  for compatibility.

* fix: use poetry environment for invoke/toml installation in CI

The validate-generated-documentation job was failing because it was using
system pip (Python 3.10) to install invoke and toml packages, while the
rest of the job uses poetry with Python 3.12.

This caused a Python version mismatch when typer tried to import modules
that use Python 3.11+ features like typing.Self.

Changed from 'pip install invoke toml' to 'poetry run pip install invoke toml'
to ensure packages are installed in the correct Python 3.12 environment.

* fix: use poetry environment for invoke installation in validator job

Fixed another instance where invoke/toml packages were being installed
with system pip instead of the poetry environment. This ensures
consistency across all poetry-based jobs in the CI pipeline.

* revert: undo models.py change, fixed CI environment instead

Reverted the typing_extensions import change in models.py since the root
cause was the CI environment using the wrong Python version, not the code.
The proper fix was to ensure invoke/toml are installed in the poetry
environment rather than changing the code to accommodate CI issues.

* fix: force poetry to use correct Python 3.12 environment

The virtual environment was still using Python 3.10 despite poetry env use 3.12.
Added explicit environment cleanup and use the full path to python3.12 to
ensure poetry creates the venv with the correct Python version.

Changes:
- poetry env remove --all || true (clean slate)
- poetry env use $(which python3.12) (explicit path)

fix(tests): flaky integration docker on enterprise

When running the integration tests with Infrahub Enterprise, we make use
of the new distributed task manager mode. This mode may introduce some
delay in message processing (default of 10s), which in turns make some
integration tests flaky.

Increase the wait time above 10s, and also make it consistent with other
places where we wait 20s.

message:
feat: allow group mapping for google sso (#7200)

* feat: allow group mapping for google sso

Google does not include groups within the tokens.
We can only fetch groups through their APIs.
One available API is the Admin SDK/Directory API which requires admin
permissions, which would in turn require extra configuration for
Infrahub.
Another API is the Cloud Identity API which provides endpoints to fetch
group memberships using the user token.

This brings several changes to how display_label and human_friendly_id for nodes are stored and retrieved. While it tries to change the least amount of code to keep code compatible as much as possible, it now stores the display_label and human_friendly_id of nodes into the database to be able to retrieve them when looking up nodes instead of computing them every times. It also introduces events to help in display_label computation.

This provides implementations for IFC-1820, IFC-1821, IFC-1822, IFC-1823, IFC-1824, IFC-1825 and IFC-1826.

subject: Allow rebase of branches during migration (#7447)
message:
Allow rebase of branches during migration (#7447)

These changes add a new flow to apply migrations (schema/data ones) inside branches. The upgrade process (via the provided command) is also updated with a new `--rebase-branches` flag to trigger branch rebases as part of the upgrade process.

A new `MigrationRequiringRebase` class is introduced with a couple of methods that need to be defined on classes inheriting it. One method defines what to do on the default branch while the other one defines what to do for all other branches.

The branch nodes can have a new `NEED_UPGRADE_REBASE` status and they also now have a graph_version property to know if a branch is up-to-date regarding the graph structure.

A new prefect event is also introduced and triggered when the `branch-migrate` flow completes for a branch.

IFC-1896 Don't query fields to compute display label/HFID  (#7731)

After the HFID and display label refactoring work, we started storing
the values for these properties as attributes in the database. We
therefore do not require any logic to try to compute them on the fly
and so we do not need to find out which fields to query for alongside
those that the user requested.

This change fixes cases where HFID and display label may not be
retrieved from the database when trying to access them for relationships
via GraphQL queries.

message:
fix(backend): do not delete rels when previewing mutation object

PR #7508 introduced a regression where relationship constraints would
not rollback the transaction in case of failures due to the introduction
of a "preview object" executed outside of the transaction.
This would leave objects with nulled relationships where it would not
have been allowed.

Make sure those deletions are not processed when building this preview
object.
Also add more coverage to the unit test.

Fixes #7853

subject: fix(backend, tests): too many db connections in integration tests
message:
fix(backend, tests): too many db connections in integration tests

Since the neo4j driver upgrade, we must ensure the neo4j driver is
properly closed and that a closed driver is not re-used.
We disabled singletons during DI to get that behavior.

A side effect is that during some integration tests that leverage local
workers, some tasks/flows depend on the injected database instance,
which would trigger new driver instances with new db connections.
Those instances would not get cleaned since it's not using a singleton
nor used within a context manager that would close the underlying db
driver.

Fix this by introducing a new class level fixture for the db instance
and use it within the injected dependency.

Signed-off-by: ub6b8c92a6359829a <ub6b8c92a6359829a@users.invalid>

subject: Cleanup docs exceptions & update deprecated resource pool mutations in documentation (#7968)
message:
Cleanup docs exceptions & update deprecated resource pool mutations in documentation (#7968)

* Update deprecated resource pool mutations in documentation

Replace deprecated IPAddressPoolGetResource and IPPrefixPoolGetResource
with InfrahubIPAddressPoolGetResource and InfrahubIPPrefixPoolGetResource
respectively, as these were deprecated in Infrahub 1.5.0.

* Update docs CODEOWNERS from customer-success to sa

* Fix markdownlint violations across documentation

- Add missing trailing newlines (MD047)
- Add first-line headings to files that need them (MD041)
- Add alt text to images (MD045)
- Wrap bare URLs in angle brackets or convert to markdown links (MD034)
- Remove $ prefix from CLI command examples (MD014)
- Replace non-descriptive "[here]" link text with descriptive text (MD059)
- Add markdownlint disable comments to 3 snippet files that are
  intentionally partial (imported as React components)

Files modified: 42 across docs, dev commands, test fixtures, and root

* Update linting configuration and add spelling exceptions

- Update .markdownlint.yaml to enable stricter rules now that violations
  are fixed (MD001, MD014, MD034, MD041, MD045, MD047, MD059)
- Add .markdownlintignore to exclude generated/vendored directories
- Update vale sentence-case style with additional exceptions
- Add spelling exceptions for technical terms
- Fix trailing newline in CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

* Add per-file MD001 exceptions for release notes

Add markdownlint-disable-file MD001 comments to 24 release notes files
that use h3 headings (### Fixed, ### Added, etc.) directly after tables,
which violates the heading increment rule. Using per-file exceptions
rather than a global rule to maintain stricter linting elsewhere.

* Fix remaining bare URL markdownlint violations in release notes

Convert bare GitHub PR URLs to markdown link format and fix
documentation URL in release-1_5_0.mdx. This resolves the final
MD034 (no-bare-urls) violations that were flagged by markdownlint.

* Centralize markdownlint-cli2 configuration and ignore patterns

Create .markdownlint-cli2.yaml to centralize configuration and ignore
patterns for markdownlint-cli2. This file is automatically loaded by
both the CLI and the GitHub Action, ensuring consistent behavior.

Key changes:
- Add .markdownlint-cli2.yaml with ignores for docs/docs/reference/,
  CLAUDE.md, .venv/, node_modules/, and other non-lintable paths
- Simplify CI workflow to rely on the config file for ignores
- Update invoke tasks to use simpler glob patterns

This fixes the issue where .markdownlintignore was not being respected
by the DavidAnson/markdownlint-cli2-action in CI.

* Remove redundant .markdownlintignore file

The ignore patterns are now in .markdownlint-cli2.yaml, which is
automatically loaded by markdownlint-cli2.

* Fix MDX compilation errors caused by angle-bracket URLs

In MDX files, angle brackets are parsed as JSX elements, so URLs like
<https://example.com> cause compilation errors because the `/` character
is unexpected in JSX tag names.

Changes:
- Convert angle-bracket URLs to proper markdown links in 38 MDX files
- Use backticks for inline URL display where appropriate
- Fix backend.mdx, faq.mdx, and all release notes with demo-edge URLs

* Expand Vale and markdownlint configuration and fix lint violations

- Add comprehensive spelling exceptions for technical terms, product names,
  and snake_case identifiers used in documentation
- Streamline sentence-case exceptions to use word-level patterns instead of
  full heading matches for better maintainability
- Configure Vale to ignore docs/docs/reference/** and **/AGENTS.md files
- Add AGENTS.md to markdownlint ignores
- Fix GitHub capitalization across codebase
- Replace ambiguous "e.g." with "i.e." where appropriate
- Fix "idempotence" to "idempotency" for consistency
- Minor copy improvements in release notes

* cleanup

* Fix MDX compilation error in faq.mdx

Convert angle-bracket email address to markdown link format to avoid
MDX JSX parsing error with @ character.

* Add baseline-browser-mapping dependency to docs

* Consolidate markdownlint config and scope to docs/docs/

- Merge .markdownlint.yaml settings into .markdownlint-cli2.yaml
- Add globs to only lint .md and .mdx files in docs/docs/
- Simplify ignores to only exclude docs/docs/reference/
- Delete redundant .markdownlint.yaml

* Remove explicit globs from markdownlint invocations

The globs are now defined in .markdownlint-cli2.yaml, so remove
the overriding globs from:
- CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
- Invoke tasks (tasks/docs.py)

This ensures markdownlint only scans docs/docs/**/*.{md,mdx} as
configured in the central config file.

* Add markdownlint-cli2 to docs devDependencies

- Add markdownlint-cli2 (>=0.17.0) to docs/package.json devDependencies
- Update tasks/docs.py to fail with helpful error message instead of
  silently skipping when markdownlint-cli2 is not installed

* Pass markdownlint globs explicitly via CLI

The globs in .markdownlint-cli2.yaml are not consistently respected
by markdownlint-cli2 when run via CLI or GitHub Action. Pass them
explicitly to ensure only docs/docs/**/*.{md,mdx} files are scanned.

* Regenerate configuration reference docs

subject: IFC-2174 Add support for uploading files via GraphQL (#8196)
message:
IFC-2174 Add support for uploading files via GraphQL (#8196)

This change introduces a new scalar called `Upload` which can be used to upload a file via a GraphQL mutation. Mutations for nodes inheriting from `CoreObjectFile` will have a new parameter called `file` of type `Upload` exposed. This parameter accepts file in `multipart/form-data` which follows the GraphQL Multipart Request specification.

The `Upload` scalar is backed by Starlette's `UploadFile` which takes care of the heavy work of handling the file itself. This allows us to have as less custom code as possible keeping things easy to maintain.

After a file has been uploaded, it will be handed over to the `FileUploadProcessor` which will be in charge of gathering details about the files, which are useful to create the object in the database. It will also call the storage component so that the file can be stored according to the Infrahub configured storage backend.

subject: IFC-2219 Add API endpoint to download files attached to `CoreFileObject` (#8254)
message:
IFC-2219 Add API endpoint to download files attached to `CoreFileObject` (#8254)

This change adds an API endpoint to allow files attached to `CoreFileObject` nodes to be downloaded. The endpoint is now exposed as `/api/storage/files/<storage_id>` and also takes branch query parameters when required. This is needed, not to actually download a file, but rather to check for the permission to download it. Endpoint name can be discussed.

This covers IFC-2173 by adding the required method to handle non-text based files. Our existing implementation of file retrieval in storage only supports text files as it tries to decode the data stream. We now have another method that just read the data stream but does not try to decode it, thus handling any kind of files.

This also covers IFC-2175 as we are making sure that a user has the permission to view a `CoreFileObject` in order to download the file attached to it. We perform a simple lookup in the database given the file's storage ID to find the node it is attached to. We then do a simple object permission check.

subject: IFC-2219 More endpoints to download `CoreObjectFile` (#8275)
message:
IFC-2219 More endpoints to download `CoreObjectFile` (#8275)

This change adds more endpoints to download `CoreFileObject`. These should provide more stable URLs. The URLs are now:
* `/api/storage/files/<node_id>` to download a file given its node ID, this endpoint is the main one as it will be unique per file and won't change when the file content changes
* `/api/storage/files/by-hfid/<node_kind>?hfid=...` to download a file given a node kind and a HFID, the `hfid` query parameter is used to specify each item of a HFID in order like `hfid=<item1>?hfid=<item2>?hfid=<item3>`
* `/api/storage/files/by-storage-id/<storage_id>` to download a file given its storage ID, it was the previously existing endpoint, its path changed

This change also introduces a `preview` boolean query parameter to force the response to use `inline` content disposition instead of `attachment` so browsers can deal with the files the way they want to instead of being forced to download them.

message:
Fix "Import Error" sync status with no explanation in the task logs (#7736)

* fix https://github.com/opsmill/infrahub/issues/6124

* Apply ruff formatting to test files

* Remove unnecessary type ignore comments from integrator.py

Since get_repository_config() no longer returns None, the type ignore
comments are no longer needed.

* Remove unnecessary type ignore comments from integrator.py

Since get_repository_config() no longer returns None, the type ignore

* Restore type ignore comments required by mypy for Prefect tasks

The type ignore comments are needed because mypy doesn't understand
Prefect's @task decorator return type correctly.

* Add .infrahub.yml config file to conflict-01 test fixture

The conflict-01 test fixture was missing a .infrahub.yml configuration
file. With the new RepositoryConfigurationError exception that is now
raised when a repository lacks this config file, the integration tests
using this fixture were failing.

This adds a minimal .infrahub.yml to fix the integration tests:
- test_run_pipeline_validate_requested_jobs
- test_run_generators_validate_requested_jobs

* ruff

* refactor: address code review feedback

- Make RepositoryConfigurationError default message generic
- Move git.Repo import to top of test files
- Simplify test mocks by replacing patch context managers with direct assignment
- Add assertions to verify mocked methods are called
- Fix pre-existing type errors with client.schema checks

* test: address CodeRabbit review suggestions

- Add assertion to verify docs.infrahub.app URL is present in error messages
- Reorganize test fixtures to improve readability by moving repo_with_valid_config
  fixture to be with other fixtures at the top of the test class

* test: fix test isolation by cloning repos per-test

Previously, test fixtures modified the shared git_upstream_repo_01 repository
directly, causing commits to leak between tests. This could lead to
unpredictable test behavior and failures.

Changes:
- repo_with_invalid_yaml: Clone upstream repo to isolated directory
- repo_with_invalid_format: Clone upstream repo to isolated directory
- repo_with_valid_config: Clone upstream repo to isolated directory

Each fixture now:
1. Clones git_upstream_repo_01 to a unique path under git_repos_dir
2. Performs config file modifications on the clone
3. Creates InfrahubRepository pointing to the clone

This ensures complete test isolation and prevents state leakage.

* docs: align fixture docstrings with Google-style format

Updated all test fixture docstrings to follow Google-style format as per
coding guidelines. Each docstring now includes:

- Args section describing the fixture parameters
- Returns section describing the returned value

Fixtures updated:
- repo_without_config: Added Args/Returns sections
- repo_with_invalid_yaml: Added Args/Returns sections
- repo_with_invalid_format: Added Args/Returns sections
- repo_with_valid_config: Added Args/Returns sections

This ensures consistency with project coding standards and improves
documentation clarity.

* style: fix docstring formatting in exceptions.py

Ruff formatting fix for RepositoryConfigurationError docstring.

* Fix mock approach for Pydantic models in repository tests

The simplified direct assignment approach (repo.import_objects_from_files = AsyncMock())
doesn't work with Pydantic models because they have strict field validation and don't
allow arbitrary attribute assignment.

Changed to use patch() with full module path instead of direct assignment or patch.object(),
which allows mocking methods on Pydantic model instances without triggering validation errors.

* refactor: replace deprecated timezone.utc with UTC

Use the newer UTC constant instead of timezone.utc for better
compatibility with Python 3.11+.

* Revert "refactor: replace deprecated timezone.utc with UTC"

This reverts commit d7c90496bf77f069a27d870f3bf4d2378d2e9abb.

* fix: resolve CI test failures for repository import tests

- Update infrahub-test-fixture-01 tarball to include .infrahub.yml config
  file in all branches (main, branch01, branch02, clean-branch). This is
  required by the new RepositoryConfigurationError validation.

- Add default_permission_backend fixture to test_trigger_repository_import
  and test_import_read_only_repository_last_commit tests. This initializes
  the permission backend so admin permissions are properly loaded during
  GraphQL mutation execution.

* fix: update tests to use new commit hashes from updated fixture

The infrahub-test-fixture-01 tarball was updated to include .infrahub.yml
configuration files, which changed the commit hashes. This updates:

- test_git_repository.py: Update hardcoded commit hashes for main, branch01,
  and branch02 to match the new fixture
- test_git_read_only_repository.py: Update hardcoded commit hashes for
  branch01 and branch02
- test_repository_config.py: Update repo_without_config fixture to clone
  the repo and remove the config file, since the fixture now includes one

* fix: rebuild test fixture with proper commit history to avoid merge conflicts

The previous fixture had .infrahub.yml added to each branch separately,
creating diverging commit histories that caused merge conflicts during
git operations. This rebuild uses git filter-branch to add .infrahub.yml
to ALL commits, preserving the original branching structure where all
branches inherit the file from their common ancestor.

Updated all hardcoded commit hashes in tests to match the new fixture.

* fix: update test assertions for .infrahub.yml in fixture

- Update file count assertions in test_find_files and test_find_files_by_commit
  to account for .infrahub.yml now being present in the test fixture
- Add .infrahub.yml to expected file lists in test_list_all_files
- Mock import_objects_from_files in test_import_read_only_repository_last_commit
  to prevent AttributeError when accessing client.schema

* fix: correct file count assertions for duplicate .infrahub.yml match

The glob patterns **/*.yml and **/.*.yml both match .infrahub.yml,
causing it to be counted twice in the find_files results. Updated
assertions to reflect the correct counts (4 yml files, 6 yml+j2 files).

* refactor: simplify mock by assigning directly to instance method

Per code review feedback, use repo.import_objects_from_files = AsyncMock()
instead of patch() for test_sync_from_remote_new_ref since we have access
to the repo instance.

* fix: use patch.object for Pydantic model method mocking

Direct attribute assignment doesn't work on Pydantic models since they
validate field assignments. Use patch.object() instead which properly
handles method mocking on Pydantic instances.

* fix: revert to class-level patch for Pydantic model compatibility

patch.object doesn't work with Pydantic models because Pydantic intercepts
both __setattr__ and __delattr__. The class-level patch is required to
avoid triggering Pydantic's attribute validation.

message:
Improve MIME type detection for text base files (#8378)

This change ensures that we take a second look at the file when
puremagic fails at detecting its type which is what happens for most
text files if we do not provide the filename in the detection process.

A fallback now runs to check if the filename is provided and if its
content looks like text (base on what the `file` utility would check).
If we still did not guess the type with this, we then assume the type is
"application/octet-stream".

subject: Fix changelog missing `CREATED` events for pools and templates (#8420)
message:
Fix changelog missing `CREATED` events for pools and templates (#8420)

When objects are created as side effects during node creation,
resources allocated from pools (IP addresses, prefixes, number
pools) or child objects instantiated via templates, no `CREATED`
changelog events are emitted. This means the changelog isincomplete:
users see the parent object appear but have no record of the related
objects that were created alongside it.

This PR ensures every side-effect object created during a node
creation (pool allocations, template children, nested combinations
of both) emits a correlated `NodeCreatedEvent`.

subject: Fix disappearing IP with mask outside prefix range (#8436)
message:
Fix disappearing IP with mask outside prefix range (#8436)

Use host address containment instead of mask-based matching in the IPAM
reconciliation query. Addresses are now matched to prefixes based on
whether their host falls within the prefix range, regardless of their
mask. Host-route prefixes (/32 IPv4, /128 IPv6) retain the original
mask check since they cannot parent less-specific addresses.

Also fix address gap calculation in the GraphQL resolver where sorting
by IPInterface instead of host IP produced phantom available ranges.

subject: fix(docs): add custom component for tab anchors
message:
fix(docs): add custom component for tab anchors

However, shared links with query parameters (e.g., ?method=graphql) require visiting the page twice before the correct tab is shown.

Root cause: Docusaurus's SSG hydration forces search: '' in the server snapshot (useHistorySelector in historyUtils.js) to avoid React hydration mismatches. The useTabs hook initializes state with defaultValue (the first tab), then syncs the query string value only AFTER the initial render via useIsomorphicLayoutEffect. This means:

Pre-rendered HTML always shows the default tab
On first client render, useState initializes with defaultValue, not the query string
The query string value is applied after mount, but any hash-anchor scroll has already failed because the target content was hidden

Fix: Swizzle Tabs component with a --wrap wrapper
Create docs/src/theme/Tabs/index.tsx — a thin wrapper around the original Tabs that:

Reads the query string from window.location.search on the client
Passes the matching value as defaultValue to the original Tabs component (so useState initializes correctly on the client-side mount)
After hydration, re-scrolls to hash anchors (since the correct tab is now visible)

Why this works
Docusaurus's Tabs component uses key={String(isBrowser)} which causes a full remount after hydration. On the server/hydration pass, isBrowser=false so our wrapper passes the original defaultValue. After hydration, React remounts with isBrowser=true, our wrapper reads the query string from window.location.search, and the original Tabs receives the correct defaultValue for its useState initializer.
The --wrap swizzle pattern is Docusaurus's official extension mechanism — safe across upgrades.

subject: IFC-2348 Webhook headers: unresolved feedbacks and last thoughts (#8654)
message:
IFC-2348 Webhook headers: unresolved feedbacks and last thoughts (#8654)

* Warn on duplicate webhook header keys instead of silently overwriting

When multiple custom headers share the same key, the later value
silently overwrites the earlier one. Add a warning log so operators
can detect misconfigured webhooks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Use safe dict access for event_data in webhook header invalidation

Replace event_data["node_id"] with .get() to avoid KeyError on
malformed payloads or manual runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Make webhook header test assertion order-independent

Relationship query order from the database is non-deterministic,
so compare custom_headers sorted by key instead of relying on
list position.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Note SDK protocols file in code-generation docs

The generation pipeline produces python_sdk/infrahub_sdk/protocols.py
but it lives in a submodule and is not checked by validate-generated.
Document this gap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Fix template pool on required relationships (#8704)
message:
Fix template pool on required relationships (#8704)

When creating an object from a template with a resource pool assigned
to a required relationship, the preview phase (`process_pools=False`)
skipped pool allocation via `NoOpPoolAllocator`, leaving the field
unset. Mandatory validation then rejected the missing field before
the actual creation could allocate from the pool.

Track fields with pending pool allocations in `NodeTemplateApplier`.
When allocation returns `None` but a pool peer exists, record the
field name. `handle_object_template` returns this set so the
validation can skip those mandatory fields.

subject: fix: add distributed lock around branch creation to prevent TOCTOU race
message:
fix: add distributed lock around branch creation to prevent TOCTOU race

The branch creation flow had a classic time-of-check-time-of-use race condition:
the existence check (Branch.get_by_name) and branch creation (obj.save) were not
atomic, and the local_schema_lock only protected schema operations within a single
process. Two concurrent requests could both pass the existence check before either
created the branch, resulting in duplicate branches.

The fix adds a distributed lock (scoped per branch name) around the creation path.
The initial existence check remains as a fast-fail optimization, and a second
authoritative check inside the lock ensures that if two callers race past the
first check, only one proceeds to create the branch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

message:
Fix false-positive conflict detection in git sync (#8849)

* Fix false-positive conflict detection in git sync

Replace the old 3-way merge-tree with naive conflict-marker string
matching with the modern `git merge-tree --write-tree` form (git 2.38+)
which uses exit codes to indicate conflicts. The old approach produced
false positives when file content legitimately contained marker-like
strings (e.g. "=======").

Also wrap the has_conflicting_changes call in validate_remote_branch
with a try/except so that an unexpected git error on one branch does
not abort processing of all remaining branches in the sync cycle.

Fixes #8848

* Address PR feedback: move test to unit tests and add news fragment

Move test_has_conflicting_changes_no_false_positive from component tests
to unit tests for faster execution and multi-Python-version coverage.
Save and restore registry._default_branch and repositories_directory
in a try/finally to prevent state leakage between tests.

Add changelog fragment for issue #8848.

* Fix unit test CI failure: add git identity fixture and use yield fixtures

Split test setup into two yield fixtures: git_identity (sets
GIT_AUTHOR/COMMITTER env vars for CI runners without global git config)
and git_repo_environment (configures repositories directory and default
branch). Both restore original state on teardown.

subject: Fix display_label backfill after schema change (#8907)
message:
Fix display_label backfill after schema change (#8907)

When a schema was updated to add a display_label, the
async Prefect backfill ran but skipped the update. The
on-the-fly fallback in get_display_label computed the
correct value during the backfill's own GraphQL query,
making it appear no update was needed. The DB value
stayed null, and regular queries returned empty strings.

Fix get_display_label to return "" when the stored value
is empty for saved nodes, so the backfill detects the
difference and writes the correct value. On-the-fly
computation is preserved only for virtual nodes (IPAM)
that are never persisted.

Fix git sync after storage recovery (#8951)

When a worker pod restarts with no local storage,
`init()` silently re-clones but never tells the caller.
Since local HEAD matches remote after a fresh clone,
`sync()` sees no diff and returns early. No objects
imported, db commit not updated.

Add a reinitialized flag on the repo instance, set it
during `init()` recovery, and use it in
`sync_remote_repositories` to trigger the import.

Two defensive fixes for the #8988 wedged-branch scenario:

- validate_node_deletions now also checks node.inherit_from entries
  against removed_schema_names and raises before any DB write. This
  closes the two-step delete path where a generic was silently removed
  while other nodes still inherited from it.
- SchemaUpdateCoordinator.execute() wraps _update_schema in try/except
  and invokes _rollback + _restore_registry_state on failure, so any
  future exception after the DB write (e.g. schema.process()) reverts
  Neo4j instead of leaving the branch corrupted.

* cubid feedback: allow templates and profiles

* refactor: restructure execute() tail so ruff RET503 is happy

Move the Phase 2 failure branch inside an if-block and put the
'return updated_hash' as the explicit final statement of execute().
Behavior is unchanged — _handle_failure_and_rollback still raises on
every failure path — but ruff can now see an explicit return.

* fixed BaseNodeSchema check which was over permissive

* fix: guard inherit_from check against GenericSchema in validate_node_deletions

BaseNodeSchema includes GenericSchema, which has no inherit_from
attribute, so iterating it crashed the /api/schema/load endpoint with
AttributeError. Narrow the isinstance guard to the three schema types
that actually expose inherit_from (NodeSchema, ProfileSchema,
TemplateSchema), and extend the existing test with a kept generic so
the loop must iterate a generic without touching node-only fields.

subject: tests: add logs dump of Redis pool state when test_client teardown hits "Event loop is closed" (#9022)
message:
tests: add logs dump of Redis pool state when test_client teardown hits "Event loop is closed" (#9022)

The class-scoped `test_client` fixture runs the real `lifespan(app)` and
occasionally raises `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` from the Redis
pool's `_writer.close()` path during teardown on CI. Every test in the
class has already passed; only the teardown fails.

Wrap the fixture teardown so that when that specific RuntimeError fires
we emit:

- a RuntimeWarning (shows in pytest's warnings summary)
- a stderr print (shows in the CI "Captured stderr" block)

Both include the test node id, the full traceback, and a dump of every
`Connection` in the Redis pool with its writer's loop id and whether
that loop is closed — enough to correlate the failure to a specific
connection / loop on the next occurrence.

The exception is always re-raised so CI fails loudly instead of hiding
the race; the diagnostic is purely there to make the failure actionable
if it reappears.

message:
fix(tests): drop fragile wait_until_converged=True from test_schema_load_and_delete (#9078)

Job backend-docker-integration (run 24860740980 / job 72785427002) failed
on the second client.schema.load(...) call when the SDK's
wait_until_converged=True polled InfrahubStatus mid-rebuild after deleting
Network/Interface and let the resulting "Unable to find the schema
'NetworkInterface' in the registry" GraphQLError escape. The actual
non-atomic-rebuild bug lives on the server (the post-delete SchemaBranch
window where deleted-kind back-references still resolve via
manager.py:437's relationship-peer iteration), but until that is fixed,
the SDK's wait_until_converged is the unguarded poll site that exposes
it.

The test already calls a hardened local schema_in_sync helper after every
load; PR #8811 added contextlib.suppress(GraphQLError) to that helper
specifically for this race. Drop the redundant SDK wait and let the local
helper do the convergence-wait it was already doing. Replace the suppress
with an explicit try/except that logs the last suppressed error via
client.log.warning on timeout, so the next CI flake names the underlying
error in test output instead of staying silent.

- CI log: opsmill/infrahub run 24860740980 / job 72785427002
- Minimal repro: not applicable (full Infrahub stack required).
- In-tree reproduction: 0/10 sequential locally - the flake is rare
  enough that we couldn't trigger it on a single dev box.

We did not locally reproduce, so it remains plausible that the same race
also surfaces with convergence taking longer than schema_in_sync's 30s
wait_for_seconds under CI load; the new WARN log records the suppressed
error so the next CI hit will tell us whether suppression caught the
issue cleanly or the timeout itself needs widening.

Refs: PR #8811 (74eb952d6) for the local helper's GraphQLError suppression.

event loop flaky test suite: second fix tentative (#9107)

* Second try about event loop fix tentative

* Linting issues

* diagnostics: stamp creation thread name on Connection

Capture `threading.current_thread().name` at `_connect` time alongside the
existing loop id/repr. Surfaced in both the pre-disconnect divergence line
and the post-mortem dump.

The loop's `repr()` is class+state only and doesn't identify the owner;
thread name often does (Prefect worker, executor pool, MainThread, …).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* diagnostics: capture call stack at _connect time

Stamp `_creation_stack` on each Connection (last 12 frames excluding the
wrapper itself), and render it as an indented sub-block under the matching
conn line in both the pre-disconnect divergence dump and the post-mortem
dump.

The synchronous stack at `_connect` shows where in our code the connect
was awaited, which complements the loop id/repr/thread name: the latter
identify the loop, the stack identifies the call site that ran on it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* diagnostics: add loop-id label registry, register pytest session loop

Adds `register_known_loop(label, loop)` and a `_KNOWN_LOOPS` registry, with a
session-scope autouse `_register_pytest_session_loop` fixture that tags the
pytest-asyncio session loop as "pytest-session". Both dump paths now print
`creation_loop_label` next to the id, and the divergence dump also prints
`current_loop_label` so the foreign-vs-session distinction is named, not just
numeric.

The repr alone only tells us the loop's class and state. With a label, a
divergence line directly says e.g. `creation_loop_label='prefect-worker'
current_loop_label='pytest-session'`, which is the answer to "which subsystem
owns the orphaned writer?". Subsystems we don't register stay `label=None`
but still get id/repr/thread/stack — strictly additive.

subject: chore: bump invoke 2.2.0 -> 2.2.1 for Python 3.14 compatibility (#9128)
message:
chore: bump invoke 2.2.0 -> 2.2.1 for Python 3.14 compatibility (#9128)

invoke 2.2.0 raises SystemError on Python 3.14 because the runtime
tightened fcntl to raise on buffer-overflow reads, and invoke's
termios.TIOCGWINSZ probe was technically reading too few fields out of
a 4-field struct. Symptom locally: any `uv run invoke <task>` aborts
with SystemError before the task body runs, breaking dev.start, format,
lint, and the rest of the dev loop.

invoke 2.2.1 (released 2025-10-10) fixes this by unpacking all four
fields and discarding the unused two:
  https://www.pyinvoke.org/changelog.html#2.2.1

No behavior change for tasks; just a patch release.

subject: convert bug-agent pipeline to gh-aw agentic workflows
message:
convert bug-agent pipeline to gh-aw agentic workflows

Replace the custom .github/bug-agent-pipeline/ directory and hand-written
workflow YAMLs with gh-aw markdown workflows that compile to .lock.yml files.

Pipeline chain, driven by slash commands on the issue/PR:
- /bug-analyze on an issue -> analyst posts root cause analysis
- /bug-tdd on the issue (or PR for revision) -> test-writer opens draft PR
- reviewer runs automatically on PR open/synchronize for ai-bug-pipeline-*
- /bug-fix on the PR -> fixer implements fix after reviewer approves test

The test-writer and fixer workflows set up Python/uv/pnpm/Node/playwright
via the gh-aw steps field so pytest, pnpm test and playwright can run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: add workflow-level gate checks to bug-agent-fix and bug-agent-test
message:
add workflow-level gate checks to bug-agent-fix and bug-agent-test

The /bug-fix and /bug-tdd agents previously enforced their preconditions
in the LLM prompt, which is bypassable by prompt drift. Restore the same
strength as the pre-conversion yml workflows by validating the gates in a
hand-written `steps:` block that runs before the agent.

Fix gate (bug-agent-fix.md):
- Initial mode: PR body must contain AGENT_TEST_COMPLETE and a prior
  claude[bot] comment with AGENT_REVIEW_VERDICT: TEST_APPROVED.
- Revision mode (AGENT_FIX_COMPLETE present): require a prior claude[bot]
  comment with AGENT_REVIEW_VERDICT: FIX_CHANGES_REQUESTED.

Test gate (bug-agent-test.md):
- Initial mode (issue): require a prior claude[bot] comment with
  AGENT_ANALYSIS_COMPLETE on the issue.
- Revision mode (PR): require AGENT_TEST_COMPLETE in PR body, no
  AGENT_FIX_COMPLETE, and a prior claude[bot] comment with
  AGENT_REVIEW_VERDICT: TEST_CHANGES_REQUESTED.

On gate failure, the step writes the reason to stdout (`::error::`) and
$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, then exits 1, which aborts the agent job. The
explanatory PR comment from the original yml workflows is dropped because
gh-aw strict mode forbids workflow-level write permissions, and user
`steps:` are placed in the read-only agent job. The user can read the
failure reason on the run page.

subject: fix(backend): make diff queries scale better for small changes

fix(backend): make diff queries scale better for small changes

This change fixes a few issues with the diff queries where the starting
point would be bad by starting at unexpected places.

An example is the (p:Attribute|Relationship) starting point for
diff_property_paths - this one would scan the whole database when running at scale.

Fix this by having separate entrypoints for both cases: when node id
lists are not null we start by filtering on node uuids - when they are
null, we start using the branch's name attribute on the relationships
(thanks to new indexes added).

scan all the nodes within the $branch_name branch (usually main).
Instead of using UNION, dynamically generate the query entry path since

subject: fix(frontend): copy to clipboard fails over HTTP due to missing fallback
message:
fix(frontend): copy to clipboard fails over HTTP due to missing fallback

The browser Clipboard API (navigator.clipboard) is only available in
secure contexts (HTTPS or localhost). When Infrahub is accessed over
plain HTTP, clipboard writes silently failed because the code attempted
the async API without checking context security first.

Use document.createRange() + window.getSelection() + execCommand("copy")
as a synchronous fallback when the secure context or Clipboard API is
unavailable. This avoids the React Aria focus-trap issue that broke the
previous textarea-based fallback (the textarea could not receive focus
while a Popover was open).

Fixes #8857

subject: IFC-2597 Add LDAP authentication foundation (#9239)
message:
IFC-2597 Add LDAP authentication foundation (#9239)

* Add LDAP configuration models

This commit only delivers the configuration shape; the runtime that
performs the actual directory bind is delivered separately.

The user-search filter is derived from the configured username attribute
unless the operator sets an explicit value, so the two cannot drift
apart. Setting `enabled = true` triggers a completeness check on the
rest of the configuration; partial configuration with `enabled = false`
continues to parse cleanly so the server still starts on any deployment.

* Add LDAP exception classes

* Add LDAP auth service interface and community stub

Introduce LDAPAuthService as the abstract base for LDAP authentication,
and LDAPAuthServiceCommunity as the no-op implementation shipped in the
community edition. The community implementation raises
EnterpriseRequiredError on every call, so the login endpoint added in a
later commit can be mounted and reachable in every deployment while the
actual directory-bind code is delivered separately.

* Expose LDAP availability on the configuration API

Register the community LDAP auth service stub in the DI graph via
`build_ldap_auth_service()`, and surface a new `ldap` object on
`/api/config` so the login UI can gate the LDAP option.

* Add LDAP login endpoint

Mount POST `/api/auth/ldap/login` and translate the LDAP service's
exceptions into the documented JSON response shapes. The community
service stub raises `EnterpriseRequiredError` on every call, so the
route returns the documented 403 envelope on every community deployment.

The Enterprise runtime delivered separately overrides the service via
dependency injection without touching the route.

* Regenerate the OpenAPI schema with LDAP additions

* Update compose and docs

* Apply polish here and there

* Fix test expected value

* Add enterprise extras with bonsai for LDAP runtime

* add origin attribute to CoreAccountGroup

Adds an optional, read-only `origin` Text attribute to CoreAccountGroup
to record the configured identity-provider name when the group was
auto-created from an external claim. Manually-created, platform-seeded,
and pre-upgrade groups leave the value unset (no data migration). The
attribute is declared with `display: extra` so it stays out of the
default UI view but is exposed via the API and visible behind the
advanced-attributes toggle.

Regenerated `backend/infrahub/core/protocols.py` and
`backend/tests/protocols.py` to reflect the new attribute.

Refs: INFP-556 T003, T004 (IFC-2587).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* add auto_create_groups settings to SecuritySettings

Adds two new fields on `SecuritySettings`:

- `auto_create_groups_filter: str | list[str] | None` — regex pattern(s)
  used to scope auto-creation. A named capture group `(?P<name>...)`
  extracts the local group name. Patterns are validated and compiled at
  startup; bad regexes raise `ValueError` with setting name and
  position attached.
- `auto_create_groups_max_per_login: int = 50` — per-login soft cap on
  the number of new groups produced; counts new creations only.

Exposes two helper properties: `auto_create_groups_filter_patterns`
(compiled tuple) and `auto_create_groups_enabled` (true iff at least
one usable pattern is configured — the presence of a usable filter is
the sole activation surface).

Refs: INFP-556 T006, T007 (IFC-2587).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* auto-create CoreAccountGroup from external claims (US1 MVP)

Implements the first-login MVP of auto-creating CoreAccountGroup rows
from external identity-provider group claims when a regex filter is
configured.

- `backend/infrahub/auth_groups/filter.py` — `FilterEvaluator` wraps the
  compiled patterns; `evaluate(claim)` returns the captured `name`
  group (first match wins, falls back to full claim) and
  `evaluate_many(claims)` deduplicates effective names within a single
  login (FR-005 to FR-008, FR-018).
- `backend/infrahub/auth_groups/service.py` —
  `autocreate_groups_for_login` runs a two-layer find-or-create:
  fast-path lookup, then a distributed lock (namespace
  `auto-create-group`) with under-lock re-check + create. Sets
  `origin` to the configured provider name verbatim, skips effective
  names that fail CoreAccountGroup identifier validation, adds the
  account to each resulting group (FR-005 to FR-011, FR-013, FR-017
  skip behavior, FR-018).
- `backend/infrahub/auth.py:signin_sso_account` — routes through the
  service when `auto_create_groups_enabled` is true, passing
  `external_identity.provider_name` verbatim; legacy path runs
  unchanged when the filter is unset (FR-001).
- Tests: unit (filter), functional (happy path + dedup + filter
  on/off), and concurrent first-login test asserting exactly one
  group is created and every login succeeds.

User Story 2 (per-login cap), US3 (default-group coordination), US4
(read-only enforcement at write paths), and US5 (events) remain
to-do — see `dev/specs/infp-556-auto-create-groups/tasks.md`.

Refs: INFP-556 T001, T002, T010, T012, T013, T014, T016, T017
(IFC-2586, IFC-2588).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

produce no matches. Previously the auto-create branch returned unconditionally,

trigger (either named directly in triggers.py ExecuteWorkflow or
transitively reached via submit_workflow/batch.add) from
`context: InfrahubContext` to `context: EventContext`, matching the slim
shape that triggers ship in `event.payload['context']`. Fixes the
`context.account: Field required` Prefect parameter-validation crash on
every event-triggered flow run.

intentionally stay on InfrahubContext — they're invoked by callers that
naturally hold the full session, and one (merge_proposed_change) needs
context.account directly for permission delegation.

message:
Auto-creation groups feature related events (IFC-2592, part of IFC-2521) (#9325)

* IFC-2592 emit auto-creation events for groups

Auto-creation now emits a structured event per outcome — created,
rejected-claim, cap-breach — through the existing event service so
audit/compliance can reconstruct provenance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(auth_groups): extract AutoCreateEventEmitter from service

Move auto-create event emission (the three `_emit_*` methods + `_safe_send` +
`EmissionDeps` + `_truncate`) out of `AutoCreatedGroupsService` and into a new
`AutoCreateEventEmitter` class with `created`, `claim_rejected`, and
`cap_breached` methods. A Null-Object subclass returned by
`AutoCreateEventEmitter.disabled()` covers the no-event-service case so the
service no longer has to null-check before each emit.

The service now takes a single `emitter: AutoCreateEventEmitter` constructor
argument and forwards through three call sites. The auth-flow caller builds
the emitter (real or disabled) and passes it in.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(auth_groups): cover _truncate boundary cases

Parametrized unit test pinning the `<=` semantics of `_truncate` around
`MAX_CLAIM_VALUE_LENGTH`. Component tests already exercise the
"longer than limit" path; this adds the empty, below-limit, exactly-at-limit,
and one-over-limit edges so an off-by-one flip in the guard would fail loudly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(auth_groups): extract make_identity helper to tests/helpers

The four component test files under tests/component/auth/auth_groups/ each
defined a near-identical _make_identity(...) ExternalIdentity builder. All
call sites already pass display_name explicitly, so the per-file default
divergence is dead — a single shared helper with one default works for all
callers. Drop the local definitions, import from tests.helpers.identities.

Also remove the dead docstring block from test_emitter.py (the test names and
parametrize ids carry the same information) and trim the AutoCreateEventEmitter
class docstring to match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(events): push auto-create event fields into Prefect resource attrs

Extend get_resource() on GroupAutoCreatedEvent, GroupAutoCreateRejectedClaimEvent,
and GroupAutoCreateCapBreachEvent to publish event-specific scalars under the
infrahub.security.* namespace so they round-trip back as typed GraphQL fields,
mirroring the AccountLoggedInEvent pattern. Add get_related() on the cap-breach
event to emit each dropped claim as a related resource with a synthetic id (the
claim value travels in an attribute, avoiding collisions with Prefect's
resource-id constraints when claim strings contain arbitrary characters).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(events): export auto-create event classes from infrahub.events

Re-export GroupAutoCreatedEvent, GroupAutoCreateRejectedClaimEvent, and
GroupAutoCreateCapBreachEvent so they are part of the public events package
surface alongside the existing GroupMemberAddedEvent and GroupMemberRemovedEvent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(graphql): add typed ObjectTypes for auto-create group events

Define GroupAutoCreatedEventType, GroupAutoCreateRejectedClaimEventType, and
GroupAutoCreateCapBreachEventType implementing EventNodeInterface, each typing
the four common fields (idp, triggering_user_id, triggering_user_name,
protocol) plus event-specific extras and a payload GenericScalar for events
emitted before the resource-attr extension lands. Wire all three into
EVENT_TYPES so the Events query dispatcher resolves them by event name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(task_manager): hydrate auto-create event fields for GraphQL queries

Add three extractor methods on PrefectEventData that read the common header
and event-specific scalars from self.resource (and dropped_claims from
self.related for the cap-breach case), plus three corresponding case arms in
_return_event_specifics() so the GraphQL Events query returns typed fields
for the auto-create event types.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(graphql): cover typed Events queries for auto-create group events

Add a fixture that mints one event per auto-create outcome and ships them
through send_events, plus a test that runs the Events query with inline
fragments for each new ObjectType and asserts every typed field as well as
payload round-tripping. The cap-breach assertion checks dropped_claims length
and content to exercise the related-resource extraction path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(events): pin Prefect wire format of auto-create event resource attrs

Add unit tests that assert the exact dict shape returned by get_resource() and
get_related() on the three auto-create event classes. The existing GraphQL
component test exercises the round-trip end-to-end but would silently pass if
attr keys were renamed on both sides; these tests fail loudly on any key drift
so events already persisted in Prefect under the documented keys stay
queryable through the typed GraphQL fields.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(schema): regenerate GraphQL schema for auto-create event types

Adds GroupAutoCreatedEventType, GroupAutoCreateRejectedClaimEventType, and
GroupAutoCreateCapBreachEventType to schema/schema.graphql so CI's
validate-graphqlschema check passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(graphql): add GroupAutoCreateEventTypeFilter with idp and protocol

Introduces a per-event-type filter so clients can scope auto-create event
queries to a specific identity provider or authentication protocol. The
field lives on EventTypeFilter alongside the existing branch_merged and
branch_rebased entries; wiring to the Prefect query follows in a separate
commit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(task_manager): apply group_auto_create idp/protocol filter to Prefect

Extends add_event_type_filter() with a group_auto_create branch that
translates the filter input into a Prefect EventResourceFilter matching
the infrahub.security.idp / infrahub.security.protocol resource attrs.
When the filter is set without an explicit event_type, the query is
automatically scoped to all three auto-create event names so clients can
issue a single auto-create query without enumerating the types.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(graphql): cover idp and protocol filters on auto-create event queries

Adds a fixture spanning two IdPs and two protocols, plus three tests that
hit the group_auto_create filter in isolation and combined. Each asserts
the exact returned set so any drift in resource-attr extraction or filter
wiring fails loudly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(schema): regenerate GraphQL schema for group_auto_create filter

Adds the new GroupAutoCreateEventTypeFilter input type and the
group_auto_create field on EventTypeFilter so the committed schema
matches the GraphQL types and validate-graphqlschema passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(frontend): regenerate GraphQL types for auto-create events + filter

Adds the three GroupAutoCreate*EventType ObjectTypes and the new
GroupAutoCreateEventTypeFilter input to the cached/introspection
types so frontend GraphQL operations can reference them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* none value management

* test(graphql): cover empty group_auto_create filter still scopes to event types

Add a regression test for the case flagged in PR review: passing
event_type_filter: { group_auto_create: {} } should still restrict results to
the three infrahub.group.auto_create.* event names even though no per-field
idp/protocol filter is set. Confirmed the test fails against the truthiness
check that was just fixed and passes once the predicate is `is not None`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(frontend): reorder TASK_DETAILS_CHECK in gql.tada cache for Linux walk

gql.tada's turbo cache emits document types in the order it discovers them
during a recursive directory walk; macOS APFS (case-insensitive) and Linux
ext4 (case-sensitive) traverse the source tree in different orders, so the
locally regenerated graphql-cache.d.ts placed TASK_DETAILS_CHECK next to
the proposed-change mutations instead of next to the other Task queries.
Reorder to match what the CI runner produces.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(events): rename auto-create event classes and reference event_name via class attributes

Renames the GroupAutoCreate* event classes to clearer, dotted-segment-free
names and updates filter/match logic to reference event_name through the
class attribute instead of hardcoded strings, removing the silent-drift
risk between the event definitions and their consumers.

- GroupAutoCreateRejectedClaimEvent -> GroupAutoCreateRejectedEvent
  (event: infrahub.group.auto_create.rejected_claim -> infrahub.group.auto_create_rejected)
- GroupAutoCreateCapBreachEvent -> GroupAutoCreateCappedEvent
  (event: infrahub.group.auto_create.cap_breach -> infrahub.group.auto_create_capped)
- GroupAutoCreatedEvent event: infrahub.group.auto_create.created -> infrahub.group.auto_created

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: regenerate docs, schema, and frontend types after auto-create rename

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* linter

* graphqlcahe

* refactor(auth): inline EmissionDeps into AutoCreateEventEmitter constructor

EmissionDeps was a thin wrapper that only proxied three values into the
emitter; passing them as keyword args directly keeps the same call sites
readable without the indirection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(auth): split AutoCreateEventEmitter into ABC and two peer implementations

LiveAutoCreateEventEmitter (real) and _NoopAutoCreateEventEmitter (null

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(auth): promote noop emitter to public DisabledAutoCreateEventEmitter

The null-object variant is now a peer concrete class alongside

* fix(frontend): align graphql-cache union type names with renamed events

The InfrahubEvent union in graphql-cache.d.ts still referenced the
pre-rename type names (GroupAutoCreateCapBreachEventType /
GroupAutoCreateRejectedClaimEventType), while schema.graphql and

Listing the specific events the emitter handles dates the docstring as

* test(events): assert exact auto-create event names, not stale prefix

The auto-create events no longer share an `infrahub.group.auto_create.`

* refactor(frontend): align domain return types on *Result naming

Group C of the Apollo→TanStack migration follow-up. Four new domain
return types introduced in ple-tanstack-7 used a *Outcome suffix; the
established majority (GetGroupsResult, SearchDocResult, etc.) uses
*Result. Align the new names to match.

- MergeBranchOutcome → MergeBranchResult
- ValidateBranchOutcome → ValidateBranchResult
- CreateProposedChangeOutcome → CreateProposedChangeResult
- AddDropdownOutcome → AddDropdownResult

No external imports — each type was used only inside its own domain

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(frontend): standardize mutation invalidation across entities

Group B of the Apollo→TanStack migration follow-up. Audit each
useMutation hook and apply Option 1 of the plan — invalidation lives
inside the hook itself unless the call needs callsite-specific context.

Adds onSuccess invalidation to:
  - authentication/login-with-credentials, /login-with-ldap
    → accountQueryKeys.all (refresh profile after auth)
  - branches/merge-branch, /validate-branch, /rebase-branch
    → branchesQueryKeys.all + tasksQueryKeys.all
    (previous callsite-level refetch only covered the action-state
     query, leaving stale branches lists in the UI)
  - resource-manager/allocate-resource
    → resourceManagerQueryKeys.all + objectQueryKeys.all
  - artifacts/generate-artifact
    → tasksQueryKeys.all + artifactsQueryKeys.all
  - user-profile/create-account-token
    → accountQueryKeys.tokens()
  - generators/run-generator
    → tasksQueryKeys.all
  - schema/add-dropdown, /add-enum, /remove-dropdown, /remove-enum
    → predicate-based 'schema' match via the new
      invalidate-schema-queries helper
  - nodes/convert/convert-object
    → objectQueryKeys.all (conversion replaces source node entirely)
  - diff/update-diff
    → treeQueryKeys.all + diffSummaryKeys.all
    (callsites diff-refresh-button.tsx and diff-rebase-button.tsx
     previously diverged — only the refresh path invalidated. Centralizing
     fixes the rebase path silently going stale.)

Marks the following with an 'invalidation-at-callsite' comment so the
plan's verification grep stays green:
  - authentication/logout            (queryClient.clear() in callsite)
  - repository/reimport-last-commit  (callsite passes config.onSuccess)
  - repository/import-current-commit (same)
  - repository/check-connectivity    (informational probe, nothing to refresh)
  - user-profile/update-account-password (no cached data changes)
  - diff/resolve-conflict            (callsite scopes invalidation to PC)
  - diff/run-check                   (callsite scopes invalidation to PC)

Drops the now-redundant tree+summary invalidation from
diff-refresh-button.tsx (the mutation hook owns it).

Verification:
  for f in $(find frontend/app/src/entities -name '*.mutation.ts'); do
    grep -q 'onSuccess\|onSettled\|invalidation-at-callsite' "$f" \
      || echo MISSING "$f";

* fix(frontend): harden auth state reset and clear cache on login

handleSignOut now resets the token and clears the query cache in a `finally`
block so a transient logout error can't leave the client with a stale token
and the previous user's cached data still visible.

Login mutations switch from invalidating `accountQueryKeys.all` to clearing
the entire query cache, mirroring logout: a re-auth (token expiry, account
switch) must not leak the prior user's branches/objects/tasks into the new
session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(frontend): promote tasksQueryKeys to standalone root

Previously `tasksQueryKeys.all` was `[...objectQueryKeys.all, "tasks"]`, which
made every `invalidate(objectQueryKeys.all)` silently invalidate every tasks
query and made `tasksQueryKeys.all` accidentally cover object queries through
the shared prefix. Coverage was correct by accident; the dependency was a
footgun.

The new root `["tasks"]` makes cross-entity invalidation explicit: callers
that need both must invalidate both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(frontend): tighten mutation invalidation scopes

- generate-artifact: drop the immediate `artifactsQueryKeys.all` invalidation.
  Generation only enqueues a background task; the artifact list is not updated
  until the task completes, so invalidating here just refetched stale data.
  Callers observing task status should invalidate artifacts on completion.

- update-diff: move invalidation from `onSuccess` to `onSettled`. When a diff
  refresh fails after a rebase (diff-rebase-button chains them), the cached
  tree/summary are stale against the new branch state — silently leaving them
  hid the discrepancy.

- branch-merge-button: drop the manual `refetch()` of the action-state query.
  `useMergeBranch` invalidates `branchesQueryKeys.all`, which already covers
  `actionState(...)`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(frontend): rename domain *Response types to *Result

Aligns the three remaining `*Response` exports with the `*Result` convention
adopted in d157dd2c96 — keeps domain return types decoupled from the wire
shape and gives reviewers a single name to grep for.

- GetDiffSummaryResponse        → GetDiffSummaryResult
- GetProposedChangeDetailsResponse → GetProposedChangeDetailsResult
- GetProposedChangesCountsResponse → GetProposedChangesCountsResult

Callers in `proposed-change-details.tsx` and `use-proposed-change-outlet.ts`
updated to the new name; an unrelated biome import-order auto-fix on
`create-proposed-change-from-api.ts` rides along.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(frontend): use prefixed schema query keys instead of predicate

The two schema queries previously used raw arrays (`[schemaHash, "schema"]`
and `[branchName, atDate, "schema", "hash"]`), and `invalidateSchemaQueries`
matched them by predicate (`query.queryKey.includes("schema")`). That
predicate would have over-invalidated any unrelated future key containing the
string "schema".

Introduce `schemaQueryKeys = { all: ["schema"], hash(...), load(...) }` and
have both queries (and the invalidate helper) use it. Invalidation now
matches by prefix on `schemaQueryKeys.all` — same coverage, no string-match
collision risk, and the schema entity finally follows the same query-keys
convention as every other entity.

Biome import-order auto-fixes on the schema/api/*.ts files ride along.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(frontend): document *Result domain types and query-keys plural export

- Add a "Domain Function Types" section codifying `{Verb}{Noun}Params` /
  `{Verb}{Noun}Result` as the canonical names and banning `*Response`,
  `*Output`, `*Outcome`, `*Data`. Convention was applied to four entities in
  d157dd2c96 + the rename commit but wasn't yet enforceable in review.
- Note the singular-file / plural-export pattern on `{noun}.query-keys.ts`
  (`branch.query-keys.ts` → `branchesQueryKeys`) so it doesn't keep tripping
  readers up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(frontend): invalidate objectQueryKeys after object update

useUpdateObjectMutation only invalidated objectItemEditQueryKeys.all
(the edit drawer's own fetch). After an edit, detail/list/count/
ancestors/metadata/tree/profiles views stayed stale until next mount
or staleTime expiry. Sibling create-object and delete-object mutations
already broadcast on objectQueryKeys.all; align update with them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(frontend): mark tasksQueryKeys factories as const

list, count and homepage lost their `as const` during the standalone-
root promotion. Without it the inferred key type is a widened array
rather than a literal tuple, weakening QueryKey narrowing. Restore
parity with details/detailsTitle/check and the convention documented
in naming-conventions.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(frontend): surface logout API failures instead of silently succeeding

logoutFromApi awaited the request but ignored the result. With
openapi-fetch returning { data, error, response } rather than
throwing, a non-2xx (e.g. token revocation failure) was indistinguishable
from success — handleSignOut's try/catch only ever caught network
errors. Check response.ok and throw with the status so callers can
react; the existing finally cleanup still runs.

The endpoint declares no error responses in the OpenAPI schema (so
error is typed never), hence the check on response.ok rather than the
error field.
