subject: fix(frontend/auth): harden token-expiry retry path (#9390)
message:
fix(frontend/auth): harden token-expiry retry path (#9390)

* fix(frontend/auth): harden token-expiry retry path

Implements PR 1 of dev/specs/2026-05-29-frontend-error-auth-improvements.md:

- E2: cap silent-refresh retry via a per-operation counter so a
  TOKEN_EXPIRED → refresh → TOKEN_EXPIRED loop bails to /login after
  one attempt instead of spinning forever (clock skew, server-side
  revoke, or a malformed refreshed token would otherwise loop).
- E1: prefix the replayed `authorization` header with `Bearer ` so the
  retried request authenticates via the header (matches authLink) and
  no longer silently relies on the access_token cookie fallback.
- A2: redirectToLogin() encodes the current path as `?from=…` and
  LoginPage consumes it as a fallback when location.state?.from is
  absent (which it is after a hard navigation out of errorLink).
- A6: type LoginPage's errors as `RestErrorItem[]` instead of an
  inline `any`-shaped annotation.
- E3: normalise the 2xx-with-errors branch in auth-callback to throw
  a typed FetchError so the catch handler sees a single shape; type
  the errors state as `RestErrorItem[] | null`.

New unit test in graphqlClientApollo.test.ts covers the retry-cap
helper (`bumpAuthRetryCount`). Also adds a one-line clarifying comment
on FetchError noting that `status` may be 2xx for "200 with errors"
SSO callbacks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(frontend/auth): validate `?from=` redirect target on /login

The `?from=` query param set by `redirectToLogin()` is attacker-controlled
once it lands on /login (anyone can craft `/login?from=...`). Previously
LoginPage concatenated the value straight into Navigate's `to` prop, so a
crafted `?from=//evil.com` or `?from=https://evil.com` could redirect the
freshly authenticated user off-origin.

Adds a shared `safeInternalPath` helper that:

- rejects anything not starting with a single `/` (blocks protocol-
  relative `//host` and schemed `https://`, plus `javascript:` payloads)
- resolves via `new URL(raw, window.location.origin)` and compares
  `url.origin` against the page origin as the authoritative same-origin
  check
- returns a `Partial<Path>` so callers pass it straight to Navigate
  without re-splitting pathname/search/hash

Also drops the old `(pathname || "") + (search ?? "")` concat in
LoginPage's state-from branch — passing the router-state's `Path` object
through to Navigate as-is removes the edge case where a falsy pathname
combined with a truthy search produced a non-routable string.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(frontend/auth): preserve `?from=` across SSO sign-in round-trip

`redirectToLogin()` hard-navigates expired-token users to
`/login?from=<originalPath>` so they can return after signing in.
Password sign-in honours this via LoginPage's `?from=` fallback, but the
SSO buttons did not — they only read `location.state?.from` (router
state), which is empty on hard nav. Result: SSO users always landed at
`/` after the OIDC round-trip instead of the page they started on.

Mirror LoginPage's resolution order in `login-sso-buttons.tsx`: prefer
`location.state?.from`, fall back to `searchParams.get("from")` validated
through `safeInternalPath`. Serialise the resulting `Partial<Path>` back
to a flat string for the backend's `final_url=...` param.

Also URL-encode `final_url` — a destination containing `&` or `?` would
have corrupted the authorize URL's own query string.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(frontend/auth): surface generic error on non-envelope auth-callback failure

The SSO callback's catch handler only set `errors` state when the thrown
value was a FetchError carrying an `errors` array. Network failures
(fetch reject, AbortError) and FetchErrors with no envelope fell through
silently, leaving the user staring at the "Authenticating..." spinner
indefinitely with nothing in the URL or UI to indicate what went wrong.

Add an else branch that logs the unexpected failure and stuffs a generic
RestErrorItem into the `errors` state. The existing `if (errors) return
<Navigate to="/login" state={{ errors }} />` branch then bounces the user
back to /login with a visible "Failed to complete sign-in" message
instead of the hung spinner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* lint

* fix(frontend/auth): preserve URL hash on redirectToLogin

`safeInternalPath` already preserves the hash on the way back in, but
`redirectToLogin()` built the `?from=` value from `pathname + search`
only, losing any hash. SPAs use the URL hash for in-page UI state
(active tab, anchor), so a TOKEN_EXPIRED on `/foo?bar=1#tab=details`
would land the user on `/foo?bar=1` after re-auth instead of restoring
the original view.

Append `window.location.hash` so the round-trip is symmetric with the
consumer side.

* fix(frontend/auth): redirect to /login on refresh failure

The TOKEN_EXPIRED path called `retryWithRefreshedToken`, which fetched
a new access token via TanStack Query and replayed the operation. If
the refresh itself rejected (refresh token expired, server-side
revoke, network error), the observer surfaced an error to Apollo and
the caller saw a generic network failure — but the stale tokens were
left in localStorage and every subsequent query repeated the same
fail-to-refresh dance.

Call `redirectToLogin()` in the refresh `.catch` so the user is logged
out and bounced to /login with `?from=…` instead of staying signed in
to a session the server has already disowned.

* fix(frontend/auth): revalidate router-state 'from' via safeInternalPath

`LoginPage` and `LoginWithSSOButtons` cast `location.state?.from` to
`Partial<Path>` without a runtime guard. In practice only
`ProtectedRoute` writes this state today so the value is safe — but the
defensive posture is asymmetric: the query-string twin runs through
`safeInternalPath`, the state-derived one does not. A future caller
that smuggles a string or an external URL into router state would
bypass the open-redirect guard entirely.

Serialise the state value back to a path string and re-run it through
`safeInternalPath`. Same guard, same shape on both sides — the cast
becomes load-bearing for typing only, not for trust.

Also: drop a comment next to the `code: 0` sentinel in auth-callback so
readers know it is forged on the frontend, not a backend code.

* test(frontend/auth): cover TOKEN_EXPIRED retry-then-bail loop

The unit test for `bumpAuthRetryCount` proved the counter increments,
but didn't prove the contract it exists to enforce: TOKEN_EXPIRED →
refresh → replay; second TOKEN_EXPIRED on the same operation → bail to
/login. That contract lived only in errorLink's switch body and had no
test.

Refactor:
- Extract the `onError` callback into an exported `handleGraphQLAuthError`
  so tests can drive it without spinning up an Apollo link chain.
- Introduce a `__navigation` holder that production reads through and
  tests can swap out. `window.location.assign` is non-configurable in
  vitest's browser mode, so spying directly on it throws.

Tests:
- First TOKEN_EXPIRED → returns the retry observable, calls
  queryClient.fetchQuery, and replays the operation with the
  Bearer-prefixed new token.
- Second TOKEN_EXPIRED on the same operation → no replay, hard-nav to
  /login?from=…, tokens cleared.
- Refresh failure (refresh-token expired / revoked) → observable
  errors, tokens cleared, hard-nav to /login. Verifies the new branch
  added in the previous commit.

Switch-case bodies in `handleGraphQLAuthError` were split to satisfy
biome's `noVoidReturn` rule and TS's narrower return type — semantics
unchanged.

* fix(frontend/auth): reject paths normalising to //evil

`safeInternalPath` gated on the raw input starting with `/` but not `//`,
then trusted WHATWG URL normalization to validate the rest. That left a
class of payloads that pass the leading-/ gate, resolve same-origin via
`URL()`, and yet collapse to a protocol-relative *pathname* — e.g.

  new URL('/..//evil.com', 'http://localhost:3000').pathname === '//evil.com'

Origin equality holds (still localhost), so the old guard returned
`{pathname: "//evil.com", ...}`. Downstream callers then serialise that
back into a string for `<Navigate to=…>` or SSO `final_url=…`, where
`//evil.com` is a protocol-relative reference and the browser jumps to
`https://evil.com`. Open-redirect bypass.

Add a post-normalization pathname check that rejects anything starting
with `//`, regardless of origin. Three new test vectors cover `/..//`,
`/../..//`, and `/foo/..//`.

* fix(frontend/auth): detect persistent TOKEN_EXPIRED inside the retry

The `bumpAuthRetryCount > 1` cap added in the original PR was dead code.
Reading `@apollo/client/link/error`:

  retriedSub = retriedResult.subscribe({
    next: observer.next.bind(observer),
    error: observer.error.bind(observer),
    complete: observer.complete.bind(observer),
  });

…the retried observable's `next` is bound directly to the *outer*
observer. The errorHandler is not re-invoked for results that come back
from `forward(operation)`, so a second TOKEN_EXPIRED on the same
operation never re-enters the switch and the counter cannot exceed 1.

The threat the cap was meant to defend against is real, but the defense
needs to live where the retried result actually surfaces — inside
`retryWithRefreshedToken`'s subscriber. Inspect the replayed result for
TOKEN_EXPIRED; if it persists (clock skew, malformed refreshed token,
server-side revoke between refresh and replay), bounce to /login and
error the observer instead of leaking the stale-auth state to the
caller.

Drop `bumpAuthRetryCount` and the three unit tests pinned to it — the
loop is bounded by construction now (Apollo guarantees a single replay
per operation) and the bail is tested via the new
"replayed result that still carries TOKEN_EXPIRED bails to /login" case.

* refactor(frontend/auth): key LoginPage error rows by content not index

`key={index}` is React's standard antipattern — fine when the list never
reorders, but couples the row identity to its position, so any future
caller that prepends/sorts errors would re-key the wrong rows and
discard their state.

Use `${code}-${message}` instead. The (code, message) tuple is unique
within an error envelope by construction (the backend doesn't emit two
identical entries; the frontend-synthesised `code: 0` row appears at
most once), and the key now travels with the row even if order changes.

* refactor(frontend/auth): extract resolveLoginRedirect helper

`LoginPage` and `LoginWithSSOButtons` were carrying the same four-line
`from`-resolution dance: read router state, fall back to `?from=`, run
both through `safeInternalPath`, default to `/`. Two identical copies
mean two places to drift the next time the rule changes (and the rule
*is* the open-redirect guard, so drift is the failure mode you can't
afford).

Move it into `entities/authentication/utils.ts` as
`resolveLoginRedirect(location, searchParams)`. Both callers now reduce
to one line, the long explanatory comment lives next to the helper, and
the open-redirect rule has a single source of truth.

No behaviour change — `pnpm test --run src/entities/authentication
src/pages/login src/shared/api/graphql/graphqlClientApollo.test.ts`
remains green (52 passed).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(frontend/auth): bounce to /login when refresh returns no access_token

The "refresh succeeded but the response had no `access_token`" branch
inside `retryWithRefreshedToken` errored the observer but left stale
tokens in `localStorage` — inconsistent with the sibling `.catch`
branch, which clears credentials and hard-navs to /login. A user who
hit this (server bug, partial JSON, schema drift) would stay signed-in
against tokens the server had already disowned and every subsequent
query would wall against the same error.

Call `redirectToLogin()` before erroring the observer so the cleanup
path is symmetric: refresh-failed and refresh-returned-nothing now both
clear tokens and route the user back to /login with `?from=…`.

Also collapse `resultHasTokenExpired` to a single `?.some(...) ?? false`
expression — equivalent, just smaller.

refactor(frontend/auth): consolidate logout side-effects behind logou… (#9401)

* feat(frontend/auth): refresh-token throws + cross-tab logout sync

Implements the surviving items of PR 2 from
dev/specs/2026-05-29-frontend-error-auth-improvements.md:

- A1: `refresh-access-token.ts` throws on every failure instead of
  calling `window.location.reload()`. The errorLink's catch in
  `retryWithRefreshedToken` already calls `redirectToLogin()` (PR 1),
  so the reload was redundant — and the reload dropped in-flight React
  Query state and double-navigated.

- A7: `AuthProvider` listens for the `storage` event and updates
  React state without re-writing to localStorage. Dropping the
  `useLocalStorage` hook here was necessary because its setter writes
  back to storage, which would cascade `storage` events between tabs
  and loop forever. Closes the cross-tab logout gap: signing out in
  one tab now drops state in the others without a page reload.

A3 (consolidate logout side-effects behind a single `logoutLocally`
helper) was investigated and rolled back: the four call sites legitimately
do different things, and three of them hard-nav anyway (which wipes the
query cache via the reload), so a unified helper bundled redundant work
into the redirect paths. PR 1's existing `redirectToLogin` already
covers the consolidation that actually mattered.

New tests in useAuth.test.tsx (3): seed-from-localStorage, cross-tab
`storage` event reconciliation, ignores unrelated keys.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(frontend/auth): tighten accessToken type + fix stale comment

- AuthContextType.accessToken is now `string` (default `""`) — matches the
  underlying state and drops a `null` union no caller relied on.
- refresh-access-token.ts comment referenced a non-existent `logoutLocally`;
  point at the actual `redirectToLogin` callback.
- Tighten the inline-state comment in useAuth: `storage` events don't fire
  in the originating tab, so a write-back wouldn't loop in one tab — the
  real cost is a redundant cross-tab bounce.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(frontend/auth): extract redirectToLogin into domain module

`redirectToLogin` was buried inside graphqlClientApollo.tsx, which meant
the REST middleware (and any future caller) had to either duplicate the
"clear tokens + hard-nav with ?from" logic or import across a layer it
shouldn't depend on.

Move the helper + its `__navigation` test holder to
entities/authentication/domain/redirect-to-login.ts. No behaviour change;
Apollo and its test now import from the new location.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(frontend/auth): REST refresh-failure redirects to login

The REST middleware previously caught a failed token refresh, logged the
error, and returned the original 401. That worked back when
`refreshAccessToken` reloaded the page on its own — but after the
side-effect removal, a dead refresh token left the user signed-in against
credentials the server had already disowned, with no redirect.

On refresh failure (and on refresh-resolved-with-no-token), call
`redirectToLogin` so REST has parity with the Apollo errorLink: tokens are
cleared and the user lands on /login?from=… ready to re-authenticate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(frontend/auth): reconcile cross-tab localStorage.clear() logout

The `storage` event guard early-returned whenever `event.key !==
ACCESS_TOKEN_KEY`, which also skipped `localStorage.clear()` events —
those carry `event.key === null` per the spec, not a per-key fan-out.
Result: a peer tab calling `.clear()` (or DevTools "Clear site data")
left this tab signed-in against dead tokens.

Accept `event.key === null` as a reconcile trigger too; re-read the
access token and update state. Added a test covering the clear() case.

* feat(frontend/auth): catalogue-gap dev banner + stabilise SSO callback deps

Implements PR 4 of dev/specs/2026-05-29-frontend-error-auth-improvements.md.

- E7: route UNDEFINED_ERROR through its own switch arm in
  `handleGraphQLAuthError`. In dev builds, emit a console.warn with a
  pointer at where to register the missing code (backend catalogue +
  frontend mirror) and prefix the user-facing toast with `[catalogue gap]`
  so the miss is visible during manual testing. Prod stays silent — the
  toast there is unprefixed, identical to the prior generic-error path.

- A5: replace the SSO callback effect's `[config, protocol, provider]`
  dep array with stable scalars (`ssoEnabled`, `tokenPath`, `code`,
  `state`, `setToken`). `config` is an object whose reference may
  change every time `useGetConfig` refetches; depending on it directly
  would re-fire the one-shot SSO token exchange on each refetch tick.
  The early-return guard also switches from `config.sso.enabled` to
  the derived `ssoEnabled` for consistency.

- E4: header comment on `RestErrorItem` documenting the REST / GraphQL
  envelope split — REST carries `extensions.code = number` (HTTP status),
  GraphQL carries `extensions.code = string` (catalogue identifier) plus
  `extensions.http_status` separately. Conflating the two is the most
  likely future foot-gun; the comment points at the GraphQL mirror so
  readers find both sides.

A8 (render extensions.code on login page) and A4 (module-scope token
cache in authLink) intentionally **not** in this PR. A8 already shipped
with PR 1's A6 — login.tsx renders `({error.extensions.code}) {error.message}`.
A4 was flagged in the spec as a micro-opt worth doing only once
subscriptions or batch requests land; until then the extra coupling
between useAuth and graphqlClient isn't worth it.

E9 (json-schema-to-typescript + pnpm scripts) was investigated and
returned to INFP-468 US2: shipping the devDep ahead of T028's consumer
trips knip's unused-dep check, so T027 belongs in the same PR as T028.

* fix(frontend): keep processing sibling errors after PERMISSION_DENIED

`PERMISSION_DENIED` was returning early from the errorLink for-loop,
silently dropping any subsequent errors in the same GraphQL response
(including a later `TOKEN_EXPIRED` that would have triggered a refresh).
Switch to `continue` so the silent policy applies only to the 403 itself.

`TOKEN_EXPIRED` and `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` still return early — they
must terminate the handler to drive the retry Observable / redirect.

* fix(frontend): url-encode OAuth code and state on auth callback

Raw template interpolation could break query parsing if `code` or `state`
contained reserved characters. Build the callback URL via `URL` +

  types and adds the runtime helpers — `isCatalogueError(extensions)`
  type guard and `parseCatalogueError(extensions)` narrowing parser
  with UNDEFINED_ERROR fallback. The fallback's http_status now reads
  from `ERROR_HTTP_STATUS[code]` when the envelope's value is missing
  or non-numeric (was hard-coded to 500 in the hand-written mirror).

  exhaustiveness check via `never`.

The frontend now derives its `CatalogueError` discriminated union from
`schema/error-catalogue.json` instead of maintaining a hand-written
mirror that drifts whenever the backend touches the catalogue. CI runs
`pnpm check:error-bindings` on any change to the schema or the
generated file — drift fails the job loudly with a remediation hint.

Generator
---------
- T028: `scripts/generate-error-bindings.mjs` reads the JSON catalogue
  and emits the per-code interfaces + discriminated union + HTTP status
  lookup. Hand-rolled in ~30 lines of plain Node — no `tsx`, no
  `json-schema-to-typescript`. The catalogue's JSON Schema vocabulary
  is narrow today (primitives, nullable `anyOf`, flat objects); if the
  backend ever introduces nested objects, refs, or arrays, the script
  throws `Unsupported JSON Schema fragment` with the offending blob.
  That's the right time to reach for a fuller library, not before.
- T027: `generate:error-bindings` / `check:error-bindings` pnpm scripts
  registered. They call `node` directly, so no TS runner devDep needed.
- T029: first generated output committed at

  adds the runtime helpers: `isCatalogueError(extensions)` type guard
  and `parseCatalogueError(extensions)` narrowing parser with
  UNDEFINED_ERROR fallback.

  malformed envelopes, payload defaults), the guard, and a type-level
  exhaustiveness check via `never`.

  `ERROR_HTTP_STATUS[code]` (the value declared by the catalogue)
  instead of a flat 500. A malformed AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED envelope

The id_token group-claim path called jwt.decode with verify_signature, verify_aud

subject: Honor INFRAHUB_CACHE_TLS_* in Prefect result storage block (#9218)
message:
Honor INFRAHUB_CACHE_TLS_* in Prefect result storage block (#9218)

Background flows hung in RUNNING against TLS-only Redis because setup_blocks()
built the Prefect RedisStorageContainer via from_host(), whose internal client
path constructs redis.Redis(...) with no ssl= argument. INFRAHUB_CACHE_TLS_*
settings were silently ignored for this one client even though lock.py and the
cache adapter honored them.

Always construct a connection_string URL from cache settings. Scheme selects
rediss:// when tls_enabled is set; ssl_cert_reqs / ssl_check_hostname /
ssl_ca_certs propagate as query params through redis.Redis.from_url onto the
underlying SSLConnection. Single deterministic code path; brings the block in
parity with the rest of the codebase's Redis clients.

Closes #9217

subject: fix: resolve S3 credentials via AWS default chain when static keys are unset (#9429) (#9430)
message:
fix: resolve S3 credentials via AWS default chain when static keys are unset (#9429) (#9430)

S3StorageSettings defaults the access key and secret to empty strings, and the
storage layer forwarded them straight to boto3. boto3 treats an empty string as
an explicit credential and skips the default credential provider chain, so S3
storage failed with AuthorizationHeaderMalformed on deployments relying on IRSA,
EC2 instance profiles, or ECS task roles.

InfrahubS3ObjectStorage now treats blank, whitespace-only, or incomplete static
credentials as "not configured" and passes None, letting boto3 fall back to the
default AWS credential provider chain. Complete static credentials are forwarded
unchanged, so existing static-key and S3-compatible deployments are unaffected.

subject: ci: scope Claude Code concurrency group to genuine @claude requests
message:
ci: scope Claude Code concurrency group to genuine @claude requests

The Claude Code workflow used a PR-wide concurrency group
(`Claude Code-<pr>`) with `cancel-in-progress: true`. Because the group
is evaluated when a run is queued — before the job `if:` — every
`issue_comment`/`pull_request_review(_comment)` event on a PR entered the
same group and cancelled the running job, even events that the `if:`
would skip.

Crucially this includes Claude's own "Claude Code is working…" status
comments: posting one fires `issue_comment: created`, which queues a new
run that cancels the very job that posted it. A single review submission
(review + inline comments) and rapid duplicate comments caused the same
cross-cancellation. Result: jobs died with "Canceling since a higher
priority waiting request for Claude Code-<pr> exists".

Scope the group so only comments/reviews actually containing "@claude"
share the cancellable `-claude` group (preserving "newest @claude wins"
debounce); all other events get a unique `-<run_id>` group and cancel
nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: ci: replace chromium netlink binary patch with LD_PRELOAD shim
message:
ci: replace chromium netlink binary patch with LD_PRELOAD shim

The E2E job patched the installed chrome binary (objdump to find
net::internal::AddressTrackerLinux::ReadMessages, then dd an 0xc3 RET over
it) to dodge ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED flake from Docker/veth netlink churn on the
runners. That offset detection depends on an exact mangled symbol and binary
layout, both of which newer Playwright/Chromium builds change, so the patch
breaks.

Replace it with an LD_PRELOAD shim (no_netlink.c) that fails NETLINK_ROUTE
sockets with EAFNOSUPPORT at the libc level, so AddressTrackerLinux::Init
takes its graceful "assume always online" path. This is version-independent
since it never inspects the chromium binary. The shim is compiled in CI and
injected into the browser process only, via playwright.config.ts launchOptions
keyed on NO_NETLINK_SO, keeping it out of node/pnpm subprocesses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix: scope artifact/generator regeneration for complex uniqueness constraints (#9487)
message:
fix: scope artifact/generator regeneration for complex uniqueness constraints (#9487)

* fix: scope artifact/generator regeneration for complex uniqueness constraints

The proposed-change artifact/generator validator decides whether it can
limit regeneration to the changed objects via `only_has_unique_targets`.
That check previously recognized a query as single-target only when it
filtered by a required `ids` argument or by a node whose schema had exactly
one uniqueness constraint made of exactly one attribute.

As a result, queries that filter by a composite uniqueness constraint, by a
node carrying more than one uniqueness constraint, by a relationship-based
constraint, or by `hfid` were treated as non-unique and forced a full
regeneration of every target in the group on any relevant change.

Generalize the determination to the same model the uniqueness checker uses:
a query targets a single object when it filters by a required single `ids`
or `hfid` value, or when every component of at least one uniqueness
constraint is pinned by a required, single-valued argument. Relationship
components are pinned by a single `<rel>__ids`/`<rel>__hfid` value and only
when the relationship is single-cardinality.

Closes #9486

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: regenerate GraphQL schema for targets_unique_nodes description

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: do not treat a required list variable as a single-valued constraint pin

A required list-typed variable used to pin a uniqueness-constraint component
(e.g. `color__ids: $colors` with `$colors: [ID!]!`) was treated as resolving
to a single value, so a query filtering by such a list could be misclassified
as targeting a single object and skip regenerating some stale artifacts.

Constraint-component pinning now rejects required list variables; only a
single-element list literal, a static value, or a required scalar variable
pins a component. The top-level `ids`/`hfid` target selector keeps accepting a
required list variable, since the artifact framework drives it per target
member.

Issue identified by cubic.

Add a node with `[["name__value"], ["name__value", "serial_number__value"]]`
to verify that satisfying the smaller subset group alone marks the query as
single-target, while pinning only the field unique to the larger group does

subject: perf(tests): cache processed internal/core schema branches
message:
perf(tests): cache processed internal/core schema branches

Registering the internal + core schemas runs the full SchemaBranch.process()
pipeline (~0.4s of pure CPU) on inputs that never change, and the component
suite does this ~1000 times via register_core_models_schema alone (53% of
suite runtime is fixture setup). Build each schema set once per process and
install an isolated duplicate per test: duplicate() is ~0ms and the cache
dict copy keeps later in-test schema registrations from leaking across tests.

Replacing the branch is only safe while it is untouched or exactly the result
of an earlier install step. If the test registered or customized schemas
first, replacement would drop them and would also give the branch the same
schema hash as every other pristine installation - the GraphQL schema manager
cache is keyed by that hash across tests, so unifying previously distinct
hashes serves managers built for the wrong schema content. Diverged branches
fall back to merging the raw schemas, preserving content and hash diversity.

Measured on core/test_attribute.py: per-test setup drops from 0.60s to 0.34s.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: ci: run component test shards with 2 xdist workers
message:
ci: run component test shards with 2 xdist workers

Measured shard wall times across worker counts (job time includes ~2-4 min
of checkout/uv sync/container setup; each xdist worker runs its own
Neo4j + Redis containers and Prefect test server):

  shard         1 worker   2 workers   4 workers
  graphql       23m00s     11m56s      8m47s
  other         20m04s     11m14s      6m35s
  core-diff     14m39s     10m16s      7m24s
  core-schema   13m31s     7m36s       6m14s
  matrix wall   23m00s     11m56s      8m47s
  runner-min    71m14s     41m02s      29m00s

1->2 workers scales almost perfectly (test portion halves on every shard).
2->4 workers only buys ~2-3 min per shard while doubling the per-job

subject: fix(task-manager): declare the escape character on prefect event label LIKE filters
message:
fix(task-manager): declare the escape character on prefect event label LIKE filters

Since prefect 3.6.14 event label filters are built as SQL LIKE expressions
that escape literal underscore/percent with a backslash but never declare an
ESCAPE character (prefect.server.events.filters._is_like_match_expression,
still present in 3.7.4). PostgreSQL defaults to backslash as the LIKE escape
so production deployments work, but on a SQLite-backed server the backslash
is matched literally and label values containing '_' or '%' (i.e. most
branch names) silently never match.

Patch the expression builder in the custom Prefect server app to pass
escape='\\' explicitly, which has identical semantics on both databases.
To be reported/upstreamed to PrefectHQ/prefect.

subject: fix(tests): pair flow heartbeats with the zombie window, shed prefect server load
message:
fix(tests): pair flow heartbeats with the zombie window, shed prefect server load

Two changes to keep the SQLite-backed test Prefect servers responsive under
parallel test load:

- Set PREFECT_FLOWS_HEARTBEAT_FREQUENCY to 30 (matching production) instead
  of 3600. The flow engine always emits an initial heartbeat when a flow
  starts, and that beat arms the crash-zombie-flows automation which crashes
  any run without a follow-up heartbeat or terminal event within 90 seconds.
  At 3600 every flow outliving that window was actively crashed while
  healthy, and every short flow whose terminal event was delivered late
  produced a failed crash action; the stretched frequency saved almost no
  event volume since the initial beat fires regardless.

- Disable the background services the test suites do not rely on (scheduler,
  foreman, late runs, pause expirations, cancellation cleanup, repossessor,
  cleanup reconciler, db vacuum, telemetry) on both the ephemeral subprocess
  servers and the prefect container fixture. Since prefect 3.7 these run as
  docket-based perpetual services and their periodic writes contend with the
  API and event processing on a single SQLite database; under xdist load API
  requests and websocket handshakes blocked for minutes, cascading into
  pytest timeouts. Triggers, the event persister and the task run recorder
  stay enabled.

Validated locally with the full integration suite at -n 4 (406 passed) and
the schema_lifecycle suite that previously timed out in CI (229 passed).

subject: improve path traversal performance with meet in the middle query (#9627)
message:
improve path traversal performance with meet in the middle query (#9627)

* perf(graph-traversal): bidirectional search for by-id path traversal

Replace the single SHORTEST-k quantified-path-pattern query with a
bidirectional ("meet-in-the-middle") search: expand a node-bounded BFS
frontier from each anchor to ceil(max_depth/2), intersect for candidate
middle nodes, then reconstruct shortest paths tier-by-tier via exact-length
canonical-split joins. This avoids the exponential path enumeration that made
deep by-id traversals hit the query timeout. Results are deterministic and
monotonic in max_paths.

Anchor resolution for source, destination, and the BFS seeds selects the
active Node for a UUID by taking the latest IS_PART_OF edge per branch/time
and then checking its status, so a migrated node's stale duplicate or a
branch-level deletion no longer anchors the search.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(graph-traversal): branch-time edge visibility + single-query BFS

Edge and anchor predicates now bound default-branch edges by the queried branch's
fork time (branched_from) rather than a flat valid-branches/at filter. A change made
on the default branch after a branch forked is no longer visible on that branch, and a
branch-local change or deletion stays local. Applied to every edge predicate and to the
source/destination/seed IS_PART_OF anchor matches (shared with the reachable queries).

The bidirectional BFS now runs as one chained-CALL query per direction (active-anchor
resolution + one CALL per hop, deduped against a carried visited list) instead of a
query per depth: ~2.7x faster on the BFS phase and far fewer round-trips, neutral when
the deep-tier join dominates the total.

Adds component tests for the four branch-isolation cases (add/delete on branch vs
default, before/after fork).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(graph-traversal): raise max traversal depth to 30

The bidirectional search makes deep by-id traversal cheap, so the depth cap no
longer needs to be conservative. Bump MAX_DEPTH 20 -> 30 (used by both the planner
and Plan validation), update the max_depth GraphQL input descriptions, and
regenerate the exported GraphQL schema. Default depth stays 5, so the deeper-BFS
cost is only paid by callers that explicitly request a deep search (a depth-30
leaf-interface search measured ~1.05s on the perf dataset).

* fix(graph-traversal): deterministic active-anchor selection

A kind/namespace migration can leave several Node vertices sharing one
UUID. The anchor resolution kept every active survivor with no outer
ordering, so which vertex anchored the search was arbitrary. Add a
trailing ORDER BY branch_level DESC, from DESC + LIMIT 1 after the active
check in all three anchor matches so traversal always anchors on the
most-authoritative active vertex.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(graph-traversal): exclude non-simple paths from bidirectional join

The canonical join reconstructs a path as two shortest halves joined at a
pinned middle. The halves can share a node other than the middle (three
nodes reaching each other through one shared hub), producing a walk that
revisits that hub. Require the full node sequence (start plus every hop) to
be all-distinct, before ORDER BY/LIMIT, so only simple paths are returned
and the cap counts simple paths. Applies to both join shapes.

fix(proposed-change): match diff action case-insensitively for artifact regeneration

_query_changed and _definition_changed compared the diff entry action
against {DiffAction.ADDED.value, DiffAction.UPDATED.value} (lowercase),
but get_diff_summary emits the uppercase GraphQL enum name
("UPDATED"/"ADDED"), so neither predicate ever matched a real diff. A
proposed change that only modified a GraphQL query or an artifact
definition node left the affected artifacts stale (INFP-409 regression).

Add a case-insensitive _is_triggering_action helper and use it at all
three comparison sites. Correct the unit and component test fixtures to
emit the real uppercase action so the regression is caught; they passed
before only because they hardcoded lowercase, matching the bug.

the builder stays kind-agnostic.

subject: fix(computed-attribute): refresh derived values after branch merge (#9602)
message:
fix(computed-attribute): refresh derived values after branch merge (#9602)

A merge that applies schema changes updates the registry via
SchemaUpdateCoordinator but emitted no SchemaUpdatedEvent, so the display
label, HFID, and computed-attribute backfills never ran on the target
branch. Stored derived values on destination nodes absent from the merge
diff stayed stale until the node was next mutated.

Emit a SchemaUpdatedEvent for the destination branch when a merge applied
schema changes, mirroring the interactive schema-load path, so the
existing backfill recomputes the affected values. The event is sent with
the other post-merge events, after the merge is committed and its
follow-up steps are submitted, so a send failure cannot roll back the
merge or skip those steps.

The rebase path has the same gap and is not addressed here.

subject: fix(webhook): open a session when loading webhook for configuration
message:
fix(webhook): open a session when loading webhook for configuration

The webhook configuration flow loaded the webhook node by running
NodeManager.get_one directly on the process-wide shared database, without
opening its own session. That caused a neo4j session to be lazily cached on
the shared connection and shared across concurrent coroutines, which could
surface elsewhere as:

  RuntimeError: read() called while another coroutine is already waiting for
  incoming data

Wrap the read in a dedicated read-only session so the shared database is never
used to run a query directly.

subject: fix(computed-attribute): refresh derived values after a branch merge (#9749)
message:
fix(computed-attribute): refresh derived values after a branch merge (#9749)

A merge that applies schema changes updated the registry but emitted no
SchemaUpdatedEvent, so the display label, HFID and computed-attribute
backfills never ran on the destination branch. Stored derived values on
destination nodes absent from the merge diff stayed stale until the node
was next mutated.

Emit a SchemaUpdatedEvent for the destination branch when a merge applies
schema changes, carrying the changed-element set so the existing backfill
recomputes only the affected values rather than a full sweep. The event is
sent with the other post-merge events, after the merge is committed, so a
send failure cannot roll back the merge or skip its follow-ups.

The rebase path has the same gap but is constrained by the scoped-recompute
design, so it is left to the coalesced recompute work.

The scheduled publish workflow calls the reusable ci-docker-image
workflow twice in one run (develop + stable). GitHub Actions artifacts
are scoped to the run, not the invocation, so both invocations shared
the digest artifact namespace (digests-amd64/arm64) and each merge job

mixed develop/stable image.

single-invocation callers are unchanged) used in the upload name and the
download pattern, and pass `digests-develop` / `digests-stable` from the
scheduled workflow so each merge only sees its own branch's digests.

subject: fix: re-validate proposed changes at merge time (#9705)
message:
fix: re-validate proposed changes at merge time (#9705)

* fix: re-validate proposed changes at merge time

Merging two branches that each introduced the same unique value could leave
duplicate values on the destination branch. A proposed change validated schema
and data integrity during its pipeline but merged using the stored validator
conclusions, so a violation introduced after those checks ran (e.g. another
branch merging the same unique value) was not caught.

- Re-run the data and schema integrity checks against the current destination
  state immediately before merging a proposed change.
- Fix the proposed-change schema-integrity check silently skipping all
  relationship constraints: it compared the SDK diff-summary element_type against
  DiffElementType values ("RelationshipOne") instead of member names
  ("RELATIONSHIP_ONE").
- Skip schema-integrity violations on a node/field that has a diff conflict;
  those are reconciled by the data-conflict resolution applied during the merge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* format

* fix: validate constraints at merge time to prevent duplicate unique values

Merging two branches that each introduced the same unique value could leave
duplicate values on the destination branch. Each proposed change validated its
schema integrity earlier in its pipeline, but the merge relied on those
point-in-time results, so a violation introduced by another branch merged in
the meantime was missed (a time-of-check/time-of-use gap).

Constraint validation now runs inside the shared merge flow, gating both the
proposed-change merge and the direct BranchMerge mutation against the current
state of the destination branch:

- New MergeConstraintValidator (core/merge/constraints.py), injected into
  BranchMerger, validates data- and schema-diff-derived constraints and
  suppresses violations on a field that has a resolved diff conflict (so a
  cardinality-one conflict resolution is not flagged as a violation).
- BranchMerger.merge() runs the constraint and unresolved-conflict gates before
  mutating the graph; violations raise MergeConstraintsViolatedError /
  MergeConflictsUnresolvedError (HTTP 422).
- merge_proposed_change records a constraint violation on the Schema Integrity
  validator so it reflects the failure; merge_branch_mutation drops its now
  redundant inline validation.
- The proposed-change schema-integrity check now compares the SDK diff summary
  element_type against DiffElementType member names, so relationship
  constraints are no longer silently skipped.

Data conflicts are unaffected: they are already re-synchronized by the
post-merge diff update, with the merge-time conflict gate as a backstop.

subject: fix(backend): normalize IPv6 host-bits input in search-anywhere object lookup
message:
fix(backend): normalize IPv6 host-bits input in search-anywhere object lookup

IPAM search-anywhere failed to return an object when the IPv6 query carried
host bits with a prefix length (e.g. 2a0b:2081:1:d3::1/127) or was written in
extended form. _collapse_ipv6 only caught AddressValueError around
IPv6Network, but a value with host bits set raises a plain ValueError, so the
raw, un-normalized string was used for the object lookup while the
parent-prefix lookup (which parses with strict=False) still worked.

Use IPv6Interface, which collapses networks and addresses-with-prefix alike
while preserving host bits, so compressed and expanded forms resolve to the
same stored value. Dropping host bits via ip_network(strict=False) would make
IP Address objects unfindable and is intentionally avoided.

Fixes #9788

subject: fix(core): cap node mutation event related resources at the Prefect maximum
message:
fix(core): cap node mutation event related resources at the Prefect maximum

A node mutation event lists every cardinality-many relationship peer
twice in its related resources with no upper bound. The Prefect API
rejects any event whose related resources exceed
PREFECT_SERVER_EVENTS_MAXIMUM_RELATED_RESOURCES (500 in the Infrahub
image), so creating or updating a node with roughly 250+ peers (e.g. a
trunk interface tagging a large VLAN range) silently dropped the whole
event: no activity log entry, no automation triggers fired.

Related resources are now built in priority order - node-scoped entries
(attribute updates, parent, the node's own related-node entry) first,
then relationship updates (which automation triggers match on), then
per-peer related-node entries - and truncated at the Prefect maximum
with a warning log. The maximum reader lives in
infrahub/events/limits.py (shared with the computed-attribute tasks)
and falls back to the default on malformed values.

Includes an integration_docker reproducer (a control interface tagging
one VLAN and a target tagging 300; verified failing on a pre-fix image
and passing with the fix), unit tests pinning the cap and the priority
order, a knowledge-doc note on the cap, a module-layout rule for
constants.py, and changelog fragment 9794.fixed.md.

Fixes #9794

message:
fix(backend): resolve diff relationship peer when schema removed on other branch (#9781)

DiffQueryParser._get_relationship_schema only checked the base branch
schema as a fallback for diff-branch paths. When a relationship was
removed from (or its identifier changed in) one branch's schema, the
peer-side path of that relationship is rooted on the branch that no
longer knows the identifier, so its schema lookup failed and the peer
was dropped from the diff, raising DiffNoPeerIdError during diff/rebase.

Fall back to both the diff and base branch schemas so the peer resolves
against whichever branch still defines the relationship.

A worker that died while holding a global initialization lock

hold it forever, blocking the platform from starting and forcing an

message:
fix(backend): roll back partially merged data when a bulk merge query fails (#9823)

* fix(backend): roll back partially merged data when a bulk merge query fails

The diff merger only discovered the affected node UUIDs after all bulk
merge queries had committed, and rollback was a no-op when that list was
empty. A database error (e.g. out-of-memory) partway through the bulk
merge phase therefore left the earlier bulk queries committed on the
destination branch while the rollback silently did nothing.

Discover the affected node UUIDs before the first bulk merge query (they
come from the diff subgraph, which exists before the merge mutates
anything) and gate the rollback on whether the merge started writing
rather than on a non-empty UUID list. Also make BranchMerger.rollback a
no-op when the merge never assigned a merge timestamp, instead of passing
a stale construction-time timestamp.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(backend): scope merge rollback metadata restore to the merge timestamp

The rollback restored updated_at/by from previous_updated_at/by for every
affected node carrying a snapshot, but those snapshots survive successful
merges. A failed merge over nodes that an earlier merge had touched would
therefore rewind their metadata to pre-earlier-merge values while the
earlier merge's data remained in place. Only entities stamped with the
rollback timestamp were written by the failed merge, so the restore now
filters on that stamp.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: feat(cache): switch NATS cache to per-key TTL
message:
feat(cache): switch NATS cache to per-key TTL

Bump nats-py to 2.15.0 and rewrite the NATS cache to use per-message
(per-key) TTL, available since NATS server 2.11. Previously the adapter
maintained a separate KV bucket per supported TTL and routed keys by
prefix into the matching bucket; the per-key expiry passed by callers was
ignored on NATS.

The adapter now uses a single KV bucket and applies the caller-supplied
expiry directly via msg_ttl, bringing NATS in line with the Redis backend.
Existing buckets created before per-message TTL are upgraded in place. The
cache `set` expiry accepts a KVTTL or a plain int number of seconds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(lock): enforce init lock TTL on the NATS backend
message:
fix(lock): enforce init lock TTL on the NATS backend

NATSLock.acquire() did not accept the token passed by InfrahubLock, so
acquiring any NATS-backed distributed lock raised a TypeError. Accept the
token and reuse it, so the NATS lock stores the same timestamp::worker_id
value the Redis lock does (and the deadlock cleaner can parse it).

With per-key TTL now available on the NATS cache, NATSLock applies the
lock TTL via the cache expiry, so global initialization locks auto-expire
on NATS exactly as they do on Redis. A TTL'd lock is released only if we
still own it, so an expired-and-reacquired lock is not clobbered.

subject: Run a single coalesced recompute on branch merge and rebase
message:
Run a single coalesced recompute on branch merge and rebase

Merging or rebasing a branch used to emit one node event per changed
node, each matched by the per-node recompute automations, which
started one process flow per changed node per family. On a large
branch this fan-out, and the duplicate recomputes it caused,
dominated the cost after the merge returned and left the instance
degraded for a long window.

This replaces the per-node dispatch with a single coalesced pass. The
merge or rebase derives once the deduplicated set of affected computed
attributes, display labels, and human-friendly ids, and submits one
process flow per affected family over only those node ids, on the
destination branch for a merge and the user branch for a rebase. Node
events now carry an origin, and the per-node automations match only
live edits, so replayed merge and rebase events no longer start their
own flows.

This reduces the number of dispatched flows and removes the duplicate
work, but it does not change the per-value writes. Each coalesced flow
still recomputes and writes one value per affected object, so the
number of value updates still scales with the number of affected
derived values. Collapsing those per-value writes into batched writes
is a separate follow-up.

Covers Jinja2 computed attributes, display labels, and human-friendly
ids; Python-transform computed attributes stay on their per-node path.
Final values are identical to a full recompute. Refreshing the readers
of a node deleted by the merge is a known gap, guarded by a strict
xfail and handled in a follow-up.

subject: fix(migrations): repair HFID values stored with non-string elements (#9876)
message:
fix(migrations): repair HFID values stored with non-string elements (#9876)

Some human-friendly ID (HFID) values were stored with non-string elements,
for example an AutonomousSystem HFID built from an integer ASN, instead of
all strings. The same object type could end up with a mix of integer-typed
and string-typed HFIDs, and re-saving an object was needed to fix it.

The cause was a pagination flaw in the HFID indexing migration. It paginated
over the value nodes while its own writes deleted and recreated those nodes,
so some values were skipped during normalisation and then indexed with their
original non-string form.

The indexing migration now paginates over the HFID attributes, which the
writes never touch, and flushes each batch. A fresh upgrade normalises every
value in one pass with bounded memory, regardless of dataset size. Every
element is converted with str(), so integers, floats and other types are all
handled.

Instances that already ran the affected upgrade are repaired automatically by
a new migration. It normalises the leftover values whether or not they were
already indexed, keeps the indexed label when the value still fits the index
size limit, and removes the orphaned old value node.

subject: fix(diff): remove stale tracked diff roots left behind by a rebase (#9902)
message:
fix(diff): remove stale tracked diff roots left behind by a rebase (#9902)

* fix(diff): remove stale tracked diff roots left behind by a rebase

Merging a proposed change whose source branch had been rebased failed
with "ResourceNotFoundError: Multiple diffs for branch ... with
tracking_id ...". A rebase advances the branch's branched_from time, so
the pre-rebase diff root's from_time falls before the new time window
and escapes the time-bounded stale-diff cleanup, leaving two roots under
the same branch tracking id. The merge task's single-diff lookup by
tracking id then found more than one.

When recalculating a branch's tracked diff, delete every other root
carrying the same tracking id (querying by tracking id alone rather than
within the aggregation time range), so a tracking id always maps to a
single diff.

closes #9898

* fix(diff): scope stale tracked-root cleanup and tolerate deleted roots

Scope the tracked-diff cleanup in _update_diffs to the current branch
pair while keeping it unbounded in time. Querying by tracking id alone
deleted identically named diffs on other branches, since a name-based
tracking id is not branch-qualified.

Skip recalculation gracefully when the target diff root was already
deleted by a concurrent diff update, instead of failing the queued
DIFF_REFRESH flow with ResourceNotFoundError.

subject: schema diff cleanup (#9905)
message:
schema diff cleanup (#9905)

* fix(backend): compare id-less schema elements by value in schema diffs

Schema diffs marked any attribute or relationship present on both sides by
name but without an id on either side as added — but only outside the test
suite (gated on PYTEST_RUNNING). Since the profiles and object_template
relationships became virtual and are never persisted, every production diff
between two database-backed schemas reported nearly every kind as changed,
while tests always saw clean diffs. On a data-only proposed change this
turned the schema-integrity check into hundreds of spurious constraints and
migrations against an unchanged schema.

Remove the short-circuit so name-matched elements are always compared by
value, and delete the PYTEST_RUNNING escape hatch so tests exercise the same
semantics as production. The core-schema upgrade path does not need the
added fallback: the internal schema is persisted at first-time
initialization, so a field newly defined in code is one-sided in the
database-vs-code diff and reported as added naturally (covered by the new
component tests).

Also stop BaseNodeSchema.update() from clearing optional text fields that
are already empty: the empty-string-means-clear handling turned identical
sides (e.g. parent "" on a top-of-hierarchy node) into a phantom
"" -> None change. The local values are captured before the merge because
the merge itself copies the empty string onto the target first.

* fix(backend): persist deprecated schema models at first-time initialization

The upgrade flow builds its candidate schema by overlaying deprecated_models
(removal markers for the old LineageSource/LineageOwner attributes, including
display_labels: []) on top of the database schema. first_time_initialization
never loaded that overlay, so fresh installations persisted
display_labels=None for those two generics and every core-schema diff
reported them as changed until an upgrade run converged the shape.

Load the deprecated overlay at first-time initialization so a fresh
installation starts with an empty core-schema diff.

* fix(backend): make Error exceptions picklable regardless of constructor signature

The base Error.__reduce__ now rebuilds via __new__ and instance state instead of re-running __init__ with only the message. Subclasses with additional required constructor arguments (e.g. SchemaNotFoundError's identifier) previously raised "missing 1 required positional argument" when serialized across the workflow engine, masking the original error.

enhance rollback query with range support (#9878)

* range-based RollbackQuery with metadata restore; unify merge rollback onto it

- RollbackQuery: per-edge-type subqueries with an explicit RollbackScope —
  AT_TIMESTAMP (unified-timestamp callers, other writers may be active) or
  SINCE_TIMESTAMP (caller owns all writes from that point, e.g. the merge
  write-block window); optional updated_at/by snapshot restore, only allowed
  on the default/global branches where vertex metadata is maintained
- DiffMerger.rollback runs the range query keyed on merge_started_at with no
  node-UUID list; the UUID-scoped rollback and GraphMerger.rollback are gone
- MergeRollbackHandler takes both branches, the diff merger, and the schema
  manager as constructor dependencies, and restores the destination branch's
  pre-merge schema_hash/schema_changed_at literally via PreMergeState instead
  of recomputing (which stamped rollback time)
- orchestrator publishes the write-block key before stamping merge_at so any
  write that slipped ahead of the block stays out of the rollback range
- SchemaUpdateCoordinator keeps exact-timestamp rollback (no metadata restore)
  and restores the branch hash/changed-at literally on failure

Part of IFC-2566 (merge failure recovery).

The cross-node getter for display labels and human-friendly ids took the

subject: Selectively recompute transform-based computed attributes on git updates (#9932)
message:
Selectively recompute transform-based computed attributes on git updates (#9932)

Previously, every Git commit recomputed all Python transform-based computed attributes for every node, even when the relevant transform had not changed. Infrahub now uses the transform fingerprint to recompute only the attributes whose transform actually changed on import. This removes redundant work on each commit and does not change behavior; values still update when their transform or inputs change.

subject: Persist recomputed derived values in a single bulk write
message:
Persist recomputed derived values in a single bulk write

Follow-up to the merge and rebase recompute coalescing work. That step
grouped the per-node dispatch into one pass. After a large merge, most of
the remaining time came from the next stage: one update flow and one
GraphQL write for each affected value. This removes that stage.

The bulk write is now the only path that persists recomputed derived
values, for live edits and for merge and rebase. It covers Jinja2 computed
attributes, display labels and human-friendly ids. Values are rendered and
saved on the worker in bounded transactions, so there is no per-value flow
or write anymore. A value that feeds another one chains as a single
coalesced pass instead of one live event per node. A normal schema stops on
its own once nothing changes; a bound derived from the schema only guards a
cyclic one.

Stored values stay the same. Only the way we persist them changes.

subject: fix: show changed nodes in diff tree when their parent is unchanged
message:
fix: show changed nodes in diff tree when their parent is unchanged

The shared nodes computation in NodeDiff filtered out all UNCHANGED nodes
before the list reached DiffTree, so the unchanged parent nodes returned by
the backend as hierarchy context (include_parents: true) never made it into
buildDiffTreeItems, which silently drops any node whose parent is missing.
Changed nodes under an unchanged parent disappeared from the tree while
remaining visible in the right-hand diff list.

The tree now receives all nodes (unchanged parents included) while the
right-hand list and the empty-state check keep using only changed nodes.
buildDiffTreeItems also attaches children in as many passes as needed, so
multi-level parent chains no longer depend on input order.

Closes #10010

* fix(regeneration): widen selection when a read related node changes

Narrowing resolved a changed node to a subscriber by looking it up as a
member of the query's target group. Unique targeting only guarantees that
the *root* of a query resolves to one object, so a node reached by
traversing a relationship is read by the query without ever being tracked
as a group member. Such a change resolved to no subscriber at all and the
definition silently regenerated nothing, shipping a stale artifact --
under-execution, which the selective path does not allow.

Narrowing now also requires every relevant change to sit on a kind the

subject: merge failure recovery improvements (#10031)
message:
merge failure recovery improvements (#10031)

* feat(backend): capture destination schema_changed_at at merge start

Add a `pre_merge_destination_schema_changed_at` field to Branch and stamp it
onto the source branch when a merge starts, alongside `merge_started_at`. The
destination branch's schema metadata (hash, changed-at) is written in place on
the Branch vertex mid-merge and is not versioned, so the range rollback cannot
revert it; persisting the pre-merge value here gives an out-of-process recovery
the source it needs to restore it. The field is optional with a default, so it
is backward compatible for existing Branch vertices and needs no migration.

The merge-start bookkeeping is extracted into `_record_merge_start` so it can be
verified without standing up the full merge machinery.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(backend): restore destination schema metadata during merge recovery

When a merge crashes after the schema graph is written, the CLI recovery rolls
the graph back but left the destination branch's persisted schema_hash and
schema_changed_at at their failed-merge values: those are plain Branch-vertex
properties written in place mid-merge, so the versioned range rollback cannot
revert them. The stale metadata disagreed with the rolled-back graph, so every
worker kept detecting a "new" schema hash and churning through reconciles.

Recovery now recomputes the schema hash from the rolled-back graph and restores
schema_changed_at from pre_merge_destination_schema_changed_at (captured at merge
start), reloading the destination branch first so the write lands on the current
persisted record. The schema load is isolated behind an override point so tests
can substitute an in-memory schema and skip the slow database round-trip.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(backend): clear stale locks and add lock diagnostics in merge recovery

A hard-killed merge leaks no-TTL distributed locks (lock.global.graph,
lock.global.schema, and the per-branch lock.diff-update.* locks) that silently
block the next merge until the 15-minute deadlock reaper clears them. Merge
recovery now clears these during recovery via a new StaleLockCleaner, deleting
only locks whose holder is no longer an active worker so a lock a live flow
still holds is left alone.

The shared active-worker lookup is consolidated onto
InfrahubComponent.list_active_worker_ids. The blocking merge-lock and
global-graph-lock acquisitions on the merge path now log before they block, so a
leaked-lock hang is diagnosable from the logs.

perf(computed-attribute): batch Python transform recompute (#10034)

* perf(computed-attribute): bulk-write Python transform recompute

Recompute a Python-transform computed attribute for a batch of nodes by
initializing the transform's git repository once for the whole batch instead of
once per node, and persisting the results in a single bulk write (chunked
node.save) rather than a GraphQL mutation per node. A node whose recomputed
value is unchanged is skipped, so it neither writes nor fans out a further
recompute.

A node whose transform raises or returns a non-string value is isolated: it is
skipped with its previous value left in place, so one failing node no longer
aborts the batch and drops the other nodes' writes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(computed-attribute): characterize Python recompute node fan-out

the kind today. This is a baseline the follow-up scoping work will flip to an
affected-only count.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(workflows): base add_tags updates on the run's current tags

update_flow_run replaces the full tag list, and add_tags built that list from
the prefect runtime snapshot, which is frozen at flow start. Any flow that
called add_tags more than once silently lost the earlier call's tags: the
bulk recompute dispatcher's database-change tag wiped the branch and node
tags the process flow had just applied, making its runs invisible to the
task API's branch-filtered queries. Read the current tags from the API
before merging so successive calls compose instead of overwrite.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

This reverts commit de6664dedeb86397315220f3326c4458ad56364d.

* fix(computed-attribute): tag process_transform runs with the branch at submission

The task API surfaces a flow run only when it carries the branch tag, and a
tag update inside the flow rebuilds the tag list from the tags known at flow
start: the bulk dispatcher's database-change tag update was rebuilding from
the creation tags and dropping the branch tag the flow had added mid-run,
hiding the recompute from branch-filtered task queries. Bake the branch tag
into the submission itself so it is part of the creation tags and survives
every later update.

An earlier attempt fixed this inside add_tags by re-reading the run's tags
from the API before merging; that doubled the Prefect API round-trips of
every tagged flow and measurably slowed storm-sized recomputes, so it was
reverted in favor of tagging at the two submission sites.

Cover the oversized-fan-out path directly: a fan-out beyond the submission

each submission carries the branch tag that branch-filtered task queries

At `large` dataset scale the computed-attribute recompute fan-out
(query-computed-attribute-transform-targets + graphql-query-group-update
+ process_transform) can saturate Neo4j's Bolt connector thread pool, which

message:
perf(graphql): skip peer hydration for id-only single relationships (#10062)

* perf(graphql): skip peer hydration for id-only single relationships

When a cardinality-one relationship query requests only the peer node's
`id` (no properties, metadata, or additional node fields), return the
peer ID already loaded on the parent instead of hydrating a full peer
Node via NodeDataLoader. This avoids redundant database work on
relationship-heavy queries such as cable-plan reports.

The resolver falls through to the existing NodeDataLoader / query_peers
paths whenever any other field, property, or metadata is requested, so
behavior is unchanged for all other queries.

* fix(graphql): skip id-only relationship shortcut for generic peers

The id-only single-relationship shortcut returns {"id": peer_id} without
the peer kind. For a relationship whose peer is a generic, the GraphQL
node field is an interface whose resolve_type needs the kind, so it fails
with "Unable to identify the type of the instance." Restrict the shortcut
to concrete peers; generic peers fall back to full hydration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015ZdYyE4JewWbMZAbvWPjQe

* perf(graphql): carry peer kind so generic id-only relationships skip hydration

The id-only single-relationship shortcut had to be disabled for generic
peers: it returned {"id": peer_id} without a kind, and a generic peer
resolves to a GraphQL interface whose resolve_type indexes the type
registry by kind. That excluded a large share of core-schema
relationships from the optimization.

The peer's concrete kind was available all along. The relationship query
already binds the peer vertex and returns peer.uuid, so returning
peer.kind alongside it costs no extra round trip. Thread that kind
through GroupedPeerNodes, PeerWithRelationshipMetadata and Relationship
so the preloaded stub on a node's GraphQL response can carry __kind__,
and let the shortcut serve generic peers from it.

The shortcut declines whenever the kind is absent and the resolver
hydrates as before, so correctness never depends on the enrichment.

* perf(graphql): skip peer hydration for id-only single relationships (#10062)

* perf(graphql): skip peer hydration for id-only single relationships

When a cardinality-one relationship query requests only the peer node's
`id` (no properties, metadata, or additional node fields), return the
peer ID already loaded on the parent instead of hydrating a full peer
Node via NodeDataLoader. This avoids redundant database work on
relationship-heavy queries such as cable-plan reports.

The resolver falls through to the existing NodeDataLoader / query_peers
paths whenever any other field, property, or metadata is requested, so
behavior is unchanged for all other queries.

* fix(graphql): skip id-only relationship shortcut for generic peers

The id-only single-relationship shortcut returns {"id": peer_id} without
the peer kind. For a relationship whose peer is a generic, the GraphQL
node field is an interface whose resolve_type needs the kind, so it fails
with "Unable to identify the type of the instance." Restrict the shortcut
to concrete peers; generic peers fall back to full hydration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_015ZdYyE4JewWbMZAbvWPjQe

* perf(graphql): carry peer kind so generic id-only relationships skip hydration

The id-only single-relationship shortcut had to be disabled for generic
peers: it returned {"id": peer_id} without a kind, and a generic peer
resolves to a GraphQL interface whose resolve_type indexes the type
registry by kind. That excluded a large share of core-schema
relationships from the optimization.

The peer's concrete kind was available all along. The relationship query
already binds the peer vertex and returns peer.uuid, so returning
peer.kind alongside it costs no extra round trip. Thread that kind
through GroupedPeerNodes, PeerWithRelationshipMetadata and Relationship
so the preloaded stub on a node's GraphQL response can carry __kind__,
and let the shortcut serve generic peers from it.

The shortcut declines whenever the kind is absent and the resolver
hydrates as before, so correctness never depends on the enrichment.

subject: Add maskless `IPAddress` attribute kind (#10090)
message:
Add maskless `IPAddress` attribute kind (#10090)

* refactor(core): make _normalize_value a classmethod

Allow a value to be checked for canonicality without building an attribute
instance. No override used instance state, so behavior is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(core): add the IPAddress attribute kind

Store a bare IP address, rejecting any value that carries a prefix length or
netmask, and normalize IPv6 to its compressed lowercase form.

Reuse the AttributeIPHost value vertex and its binary index by returning
AttributeDBNodeType.IPHOST, so no graph schema change, index or migration is
needed. prefixlen is written as the family maximum because a bare address is a
single host and neo4j refuses to MERGE on a null property; it is deliberately
absent from the GraphQL type and from get_allowed_property_in_path.

Values sort lexically rather than numerically, since the shared binary index is
only reachable through IPAM's own queries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(schema): reject non-canonical values when changing an attribute kind

A kind change does not rewrite stored values, so switching an attribute to
IPHost left a bare 10.0.0.1 in the database where the canonical form is
10.0.0.1/32, making value filters and uniqueness comparisons match a stale
string. Flag any stored value that is not already canonical for the new kind.

The check needs no list of the kinds it applies to: kinds that do not normalize
inherit an identity _normalize_value, so it is a no-op for them and covers a
future normalizing kind for free. In practice it applies to IPHost, IPNetwork,
IPAddress and MacAddress.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(generated): regenerate schema, docs and frontend types for IPAddress

Output of backend.generate, schema.generate-graphqlschema,
schema.generate-jsonschema, docs.generate and the frontend codegen.

The graphql-cache.d.ts churn is gql.tada rehashing every cached document
because the schema changed; none of it is specific to the new kind.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(frontend): support the IPAddress attribute kind

Register the kind so it renders as a plain text input in object forms, shows as
a column in list views, and offers a text filter. The four switches it is added
to fall through to warnUnexpectedType and render nothing for an unknown kind, so
each case is what keeps the field from silently disappearing.

Validate the value in the form as well, since a prefixed address is a mistake
worth catching before the round trip: a value containing a slash is reported as
needing a bare address, and anything else malformed as an invalid IPv4 or IPv6
address. Leading zeros are rejected to match the backend.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: document the IPAddress attribute kind

Add the kind to the hand-written kind list and the UI-behaviour table, and note
on the IPHost entry that it stores a prefix so the two read as distinct choices.

Record in the knowledge doc that _normalize_value is a classmethod so a value
can be checked without an attribute instance, and that a kind change is only
allowed when the stored values are already canonical for the new kind.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(sdk): bump python_sdk for the IPAddress attribute kind

Advances python_sdk to the latest infrahub-develop and adds the generated
IPAddress attribute-kind models, which unblocks the SDK node tests for a bare
address.

The pointer spans 14 upstream commits as well as the IPAddress change, mostly
the infrahubctl schema-format work, so an unrelated SDK regression bisected to
this commit most likely comes from those.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(frontend): count IPv6 groups correctly in the IPAddress validator

A trailing dotted quad carries 32 bits, so it stands for the final two groups
rather than one. Counting it as one rejected valid addresses such as
1:2:3:4:5:6:1.2.3.4. Allowing eight explicit groups alongside a "::" run also
accepted invalid ones such as ::1:2:3:4:5:6:7:8, since the run has to stand for
at least one group of zeros.

The accept and reject cases are checked against ipaddress.ip_address so the form
validation and the backend agree on the same inputs.

Also refresh the betterer results: adding IPAddress to ATTRIBUTE_KIND changed the
content hashes of the two switch files and the text of several recorded errors
that embed the AttributeKind union, which the CI-mode check treats as a change
even though the error count is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
